section_about:
We are looking for a Senior Manager, 3P Revenue Accounting & Reporting to join our Accounting team.
You will own revenue recognition, month-end close and reporting for Claude sold through our cloud service provider (CSP) channels: AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud Vertex AI and Microsoft Azure Marketplace.
These channels are among the fastest-growing revenue streams at the company.
They run on consumption-based, partner-reported data that changes every month.
You will be the accounting point of contact for the finance and partner teams at AWS, Google and Microsoft.
Internally, you will partner with Finance, FAB, Engineering and business teams to turn partner billing feeds into accurate, auditable revenue.
You will also lead the automation of a close that is still heavily manual.
If you want to build the financial infrastructure behind a fast-growing AI company, come join us in our mission to build safe, beneficial AI.
section_responsibilities:
Lead the revenue close for cloud service provider Marketplace within a listed company timeline.
Prepare and review revenue, revenue-share, reserve journal entries, accruals and true-ups including memos for accounting assessments and judgments.
Own balance sheet reconciliations, reserves, and the usage-to-invoice-to-cash bridge.
Perform monthly and quarterly flux analysis and prepare flux decks for leadership.
Own quarter-end deliverables, including footnote disclosures, flux commentary and presentations to leadership and Corporate Accounting.
Serve as the primary contact for external auditors.
Review the work of accountants and contractors, set the close calendar, and keep close packages complete and audit-ready.
Own monthly and quarterly 3P revenue reporting for leadership and FP&A, by partner, model, product, region and customer.
Review partner usage, invoice, disbursement and fraud reports each month, and resolve data issues before close.
Serve as the accounting point of contact for the finance, engineering and product teams and drive reporting improvements that support an on-time close.
Apply ASC 606 to 3P arrangements, including principal-vs-agent, variable consideration and reseller arrangements.
Estimate and document reserves, including credit loss (ASC 326).
Assess the accounting for new 3P products, programs and billing changes, partnering with Technical Accounting on complex judgments.
Partner with the Engineering teams to automate manual close processes, including SQL-driven workbooks, automated reconciliations and system-generated journal entries.
Own 3P SOX controls, including design, documentation, gap remediation and audit evidence.
Partner with FP&A, Treasury, AR and business teams on forecasts, cash and partner disputes.

Have managed external partner relationships where you depended on their data, and pushed for fixes.
Have strong SQL skills (BigQuery or similar) and experience automating close workbooks or reconciliations.
Have designed or operated SOX controls and supported external audits.
Communicate clearly with accounting, finance, business and engineering teams.
Thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built.

A Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA or equivalent (ACA, ACCA).
Big 4 audit experience combined with industry experience at a high-growth tech or SaaS company.
Experience with cloud marketplace, reseller or channel revenue (AWS Marketplace, Google Cloud Marketplace, Azure Marketplace).
Experience with usage-based and subscription revenue models.
Hands-on experience with Workday Financials, NetSuite, Numeric, Hex or similar close and reporting tools.

Experience using AI tools to automate accounting and reporting work.

location: San Francisco, CA; New York City, NY
section_about:
Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team brings Claude to organizations doing some of the world's most important work across the nonprofit and education sectors.
These organizations share a problem: mission-critical work, thin budgets, and little slack to figure out new technology on their own.
Our Customer Success team helps them go from first login to Claude being part of how their teams work, but we cannot do that one organization at a time, nor should we.
The sector already has trusted intermediaries these organizations turn to first: networks, capacity builders, funder technical assistance providers, community colleges, and fellowship programs.
This role exists to make those intermediaries as effective at activating and training organizations on Claude as our own Customer Success team is.
As the Scaled Enablement Lead, you'll build the Claude for Nonprofits train-the-trainer program that qualifies intermediaries to onboard organizations and deliver Anthropic-designed workshops on our behalf.
You'll own the kits, credentials, and quality gates that let them run the show without an Anthropic CSM in the room.
You'll also own the enablement thinking behind scaling impact through Claude Corps: how what fellows learn and build serves every organization we support, not only the ones that host them.
The people you enable are not selling Claude.
They are trainers, implementers, and program staff whose job is to help mission-driven organizations meaningfully adopt AI.
Your job is to make sure these intermediaries can do that with Claude, to the same bar we hold ourselves to, and to help them evolve their offerings as we learn what these organizations need.
The measure of success for this role is organizations activated and trained well without Anthropic delivering it.
You'll be half program builder, half facilitator.
You'll design and deliver the first cohorts yourself, then make the system repeatable: kits, qualification paths, credentials, teach-back gates, and a refresh rhythm that keeps content current as our products change.
You'll build on the operating model and certification infrastructure of Anthropic's Education team and own everything specific to this audience, working closely with Beneficial Deployments Customer Success, Partnerships, Claude Corps program leadership, and our Education teams.
This is not a partner account management or alliances role, and it carries no quota.
It is not a book-of-business Customer Success role either, though you'll spend time with organizations to stay grounded in what these nonprofits truly need.
The role reports to the Customer Success Lead for Beneficial Deployments, has no direct reports today, and may grow into people management as the program scales.
Expect periodic travel for in-person cohorts and sessions.

Build the kits intermediaries teach from: an activation playbook covering kickoff, admin setup, launch, and Day 30/60/90 reviews, and workshop-in-a-box modules starting with AI fluency and use case discovery, each with a deck, facilitator guide, demo scripts, sample data, and workbook
Recruit and qualify a pilot cohort of anchor intermediaries, then open a repeatable application process that routes each to the right track and the right home, whether the Claude Partner Network or a Beneficial Deployments credential
Design and deliver enablement for network intermediaries, adapting the program to how each reaches and supports its members, and help them evolve their offerings as we learn what organizations need
Build the connective tissue among intermediaries so they learn from each other: shared office hours, a facilitator cohort that stays together after qualification, and a clear path for bringing new intermediaries along

job_title: Security Engineer / Research Engineer, RL Security
location: San Francisco, CA; New York City, NY; Seattle, WA
section_about:
Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons.
At frontier scale, an RL run is a large distributed system: training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts.
As an engineer in RL Engineering, you'll work on keeping that system secure as it scales.
This is a hands-on engineering role.
You'll work in the RL codebase and the infrastructure underneath it, alongside the engineers and researchers who build and use it.
The system is large and changes as fast as the research does, so security work here has to keep up with that pace without costing performance or velocity.
We're hiring from two backgrounds: security engineers who want to work on large-scale ML systems, and ML systems or research engineers who want to work on security.
Strong candidates have depth in one and real interest in the other.
section_responsibilities:
Design, build, and operate security controls for RL training systems and the infrastructure they run on
Work across the stack (orchestration, environments, training, inference) wherever the work is needed
Review designs and code across the RL stack, find security problems, and fix them
Build shared libraries and tooling that other RL engineers and researchers build on
Build the observability needed to understand what these systems are doing
Work with researchers and performance engineers to make sure security changes preserve training correctness and performance
Write clear design documents for what you build
section_requirements:
Strong software engineering skills in Python and at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or Go
Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or security systems in production
Strong understanding of security fundamentals
Working knowledge of Linux, containers, and cloud infrastructure
Experience debugging complex problems across many hosts and services
Ability to reason about tradeoffs between security, performance, and reliability
Strong written communication, including design documents
section_preferred:
Experience running ML training or inference infrastructure at scale
Experience with infrastructure security, such as isolation, access control, networking, or identity
Experience with container orchestration such as Kubernetes, and with sandboxed or virtualized code execution at scale
Experience building observability for large fleets
Experience supporting research teams or other fast-moving internal users
Familiarity with reinforcement learning or large language model training workloads

Promuoverai l'adozione di un'IA di frontiera e sicura concludendo accordi strategici con ministeri e amministrazioni centrali, amministrazioni regionali e locali ed enti pubblici.
Metterai la tua esperienza di vendita consulenziale nel settore pubblico al servizio della crescita dei ricavi, diventando un partner di fiducia per gli interlocutori del settore e aiutandoli a integrare e adottare l'IA e a scoprirne tutte le potenzialità nei servizi ai cittadini, nell'amministrazione e nella ricerca.
In collaborazione con i team GTM, Prodotto e Marketing, perfezionerai costantemente la nostra proposta di valore, la nostra metodologia di vendita e il nostro posizionamento, perché siano rilevanti per chi prende le decisioni nel settore pubblico.
Il profilo ideale ha la passione per lo sviluppo di nuovi segmenti di mercato, per l'individuazione delle opportunità ad alto potenziale e per l'attuazione delle strategie necessarie a coglierle.
Favorendo la diffusione dei prodotti emergenti di Anthropic, aiuterai le istituzioni pubbliche ad acquisire nuove capacità, contribuendo al tempo stesso allo sviluppo etico dell'IA.
Responsabilità:
Acquisire nuovi clienti e generare ricavi per Anthropic nel settore pubblico in Italia.
Orientarti all'interno di istituzioni pubbliche complesse per raggiungere le figure decisionali chiave, far conoscere i nostri servizi e aiutarle ad avere successo con Anthropic.
Sarai responsabile dell'intero ciclo di vendita, dal primo contatto alla chiusura.
Definire e attuare strategie di vendita innovative, adatte ai cicli degli appalti pubblici e ai processi di bilancio, comprese gare, accordi quadro e canali di vendita tramite partner o rivenditori, per raggiungere e superare gli obiettivi di fatturato.
Analizzare lo scenario, le tendenze e le dinamiche del settore pubblico per tradurre i piani strategici in attività e campagne commerciali mirate.
Guidare l'espansione sul mercato individuando nuovi casi d'uso all'interno di ministeri, enti e uffici amministrativi.
Collaborare in modo trasversale per differenziare la nostra offerta per le applicazioni del settore pubblico.
Muoverti in ecosistemi complessi di interlocutori del settore pubblico (dirigenti apicali, responsabili della trasformazione digitale e della tecnologia, direzioni IT e uffici acquisti) per costruire consenso.

Contribuire alla roadmap e alle funzionalità di prodotto raccogliendo il feedback di chi utilizza le nostre soluzioni nel settore pubblico e portandone all'interno le esigenze.
Fornire indicazioni che rafforzino la nostra proposta di valore per le istituzioni pubbliche.
Perfezionare costantemente la metodologia di vendita per il settore pubblico, integrando quanto appreso in playbook, modelli e buone pratiche.
Individuare miglioramenti di processo che ottimizzino la produttività e la coerenza commerciale.

Una comprovata esperienza nella gestione di cicli di vendita complessi all'interno di istituzioni pubbliche e nella conclusione di accordi strategici, fondata sulla comprensione sia dei requisiti tecnici sia dei casi d'uso del settore pubblico
Una padronanza concreta degli appalti pubblici italiani: gare, accordi quadro, centrali di committenza e canali di vendita tramite partner o rivenditori
Una capacità dimostrata di muoverti nelle strutture organizzative del settore pubblico, costruendo consenso tra interlocutori diversi, tra cui dirigenti apicali, responsabili della trasformazione digitale e della tecnologia e direzioni IT
Un'esperienza comprovata nel superare gli obiettivi di fatturato grazie a una gestione efficace di una pipeline e di un processo di vendita in continua evoluzione
Eccellenti capacità di comunicazione e la sicurezza necessaria per presentare a interlocutori diversi del settore pubblico, dai team tecnici ai dirigenti apicali
Una conoscenza approfondita dei cicli di acquisto, dei processi decisionali e delle principali criticità del settore pubblico, compresi i requisiti di sovranità dei dati, sicurezza e conformità normativa
Un approccio strategico e analitico al mercato del settore pubblico, unito a un'esecuzione tattica e creativa per cogliere le opportunità
Padronanza dell'italiano e dell'inglese a livello bilingue, con un'eccellente comunicazione scritta e orale in entrambe le lingue
Passione per i sistemi di IA avanzati e le loro applicazioni, o esperienza diretta con essi.

section_about:
Platform Safety builds the infrastructure that lets Anthropic bring its most capable models to more people, safely and securely.
Our systems decide both who can access our most advanced models, and what capabilities they can access, wherever Claude is available.
That includes identity and business verification, trusted access programs, and the core services that grant, hold and enforce model access across our products.
These systems already power the Cyber Verification Program, which now includes Project Glasswing, and the Life Sciences Verification Program with further more advanced use cases in development.
As a Staff+ engineer, you'll help set the technical direction for this work.
The foundations are live and adoption is growing quickly, so the next challenge is scale: making access a matter of configuration instead of code, making verification reusable, and giving customers a consistent experience on every surface.
You'll work closely with safeguards, product, design and research to turn safety policy into systems that are easy to use and enforce.
You'll also take new 0 → 1 efforts from idea to delivery as new capabilities and programs emerge.
section_responsibilities:
You'll design, build and operate the systems that decide who gets access to our most capable models.

You'll build out our identity and business verification system (KYC/KYB) as a reusable service that any program can use, which means integrating verification vendors, protecting sensitive personal data, expanding into new regions, and building fair review and appeal paths for customers.
You'll also evolve the core services behind every access decision, including the services that grant and hold access and the customer and user identity models they rely on, and keep them highly available and consistent across our own products and cloud platforms.
You'll shape the architecture through clear written proposals, review key designs, and mentor engineers on a growing team.
You'll also share on-call, lead incident response, and support emerging new programs.

location: San Francisco, CA; New York City, NY
section_about:
Anthropic is seeking a Financial Data and Controls Lead to join our Billing Platform team.
Billing Platform builds the systems customers use to transact with Anthropic: subscriptions, usage billing, quote to cash, invoicing, and payments.
You'll be the dedicated owner of billing accuracy, reconciliation, and financial controls across those systems, making sure the right checks run, the right controls are in place, and the audit evidence exists.
Our billing systems and pricing change often, and each flow needs to meet SOX requirements.
Accurate billing is what lets us launch products and pricing quickly and still close the books on time.
The hard problems today include validating negotiated pricing from contract to invoice, handling the many forms of credits, app store billing, and keeping controls current while the systems under them are replaced.
This is a foundational role and the first hire of its kind on the team.
You'll lead a working group of the reconciliation and controls owners from each billing engineering team, and you'll set the approach they follow.
You'll work closely with Finance Systems, Accounting, Internal Audit, and Data Engineering.
The role sits in Engineering and works with Finance every day.
Our Data organization builds the pipelines and owns the warehouse, and you'll use that data and partner with that team.
We're looking for an engineer or data practitioner with strong accounting domain knowledge, who can talk to engineers about systems and to Finance and auditors about risk and materiality.
section_responsibilities:
Own reconciliation and accuracy checks for critical billing data (quantity, price, discounts, and invoices) across our product platform, third-party billing and payment providers, app stores, cloud marketplaces, and in-house systems
Design and run detective controls that catch billing errors before they reach the accounting books

Review billing changes that have financial impact, flag the ones that touch SOX or IT application controls (ITACs), and make sure functional test evidence is in place

Triage billing errors, prioritize backfills and fixes with the owning teams, and track materiality over time
Define and maintain the data contracts between billing and finance systems, so downstream teams can find and trust the data they need
Lead the working group of reconciliation and controls owners across billing engineering teams, through influence and not reporting lines

Join Anthropic as an EMEA-based Customer Success Manager supporting our Beneficial Deployments team's work with nonprofits.
You'll be a strategic partner and trusted advisor to mission-driven organizations across EMEA, spanning a range of impact areas.
Your focus is driving activation, adoption, and value of Claude across Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and the API.
That means helping these organizations evolve how they work internally, and guiding them as they evolve how they serve their missions and constituents with AI.

Within the pod, you'll decide what level of engagement each customer most needs and either personally deliver it or connect the customer to resources that serve their needs.
CS-led engagements range from high-touch 1:1 partnerships to one-to-many cohort engagements, with the latitude to design other approaches where they serve customers better.
As one of our early Customer Success Managers in EMEA, you'll be a pioneer: helping to build regional processes, establish new customer relationships, and represent Anthropic's brand in a high-growth market.
You'll operate with significant autonomy while staying closely aligned with global teams, which calls for someone who thrives in ambiguous environments and works effectively across time zones.
The insights you gather from these partnerships will directly inform our research priorities, product development, and strategies for beneficial AI deployment.
As the voice of the customer, you'll help shape how we build and deliver AI systems that amplify social good.

section_about:
Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us.
DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it.
Security at that scale runs on data, and you'll be the engineer who owns it and the systems that produce it: component-level hardware inventory and chain of custody, fed by software that runs at our sites and on hosts, and continuous control monitoring, with the posture calculations that decide what each site is cleared to run.
You set the architecture, agree schemas and interfaces with the teams, operators and vendors that own the sources, build the pipelines, stores and tools, and run what you ship.
The goal is security that runs itself: custody, access and evidence verified continuously from records, with tools and AI agents doing the reviews.
We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones.
We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well.
You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's compute and data center operations teams, and directly with data center operators, hardware vendors and logistics providers.
The role is based in San Francisco, with remote applicants in the US considered, and involves regular travel to data center sites, which are critical infrastructure.
section_responsibilities:
Hardware inventory and chain of custody: own the component-level record of what hardware exists, where it is and who has handled it: the data model, the pipelines that join inventory and custody events from many source systems, change history on every record, and the tamper-evident stores behind it
Tools, automation and AI agents: build the tools and agents the team runs on this data: reconciliation, audit evidence exports, custody checks.
When a review keeps costing people time, you build the tool or agent that retires it
Custody workflows and field software: build the workflows and the site and host software that capture custody events as they happen (a receipt, a move, a data wipe, a decommission) and enforce who is authorized to record them
Continuous control monitoring and posture: own the pipelines that turn check outcomes, assessment results and findings into per-control and per-site measures over time, against the compliance frameworks we and our partners are assessed against, and the posture calculation that decides what a site is cleared to run
Data quality: build coverage checks, reconciliation against sources and alerts on a silent or drifting feed, so a wrong or missing record is caught the same day; own retention and access controls on the records
Integration and reporting: agree schemas and interfaces with the engineers who run the security monitoring platform, and build the query surfaces and reports the team, site leads and leadership use directly

section_about:
Claude is trained and served on hardware in data centers Anthropic operates and in sites partners build and run for us.
DCSE secures that footprint: the sites, the hardware moving through them, and the people and vendors who touch it.
You'll be the engineer who owns autonomous systems across that footprint as one security domain, from both sides: drones, ground robots and automated vehicles for patrol, inspection and moving hardware, including the security of that automation inside secure areas, and the detection systems that tell us what is flying over or operating near a site uninvited.
You set the approach, select and integrate the platforms and sensors, write the requirements vendors build to, and run what you ship, from the operating model where operators assign missions and machines carry them out to the playbook that turns a detection into an identified track and a well-evidenced handoff to whoever holds authority over the airspace.
Interdiction is not part of this role.
The goal is security that runs itself: coverage, fleet health and evidence verified continuously, with tools and AI agents doing the routine triage.
We favor simple, standard controls and tools that can be verified over elaborate ones.
We use Claude throughout our engineering workflow and expect you to as well.
You'll work with the rest of DCSE, including its physical security systems engineers and the engineers on its security monitoring platform, with Anthropic's data center operations and legal teams, and directly with site operators, equipment vendors and aviation and public safety authorities.

section_about:
We are looking for an experienced accountant to own Equity Accounting and Reporting at Anthropic, based in San Francisco.
You will be the one owner of equity accounting numbers across US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP in every jurisdiction where we have employees holding equity: expense booking by entity, intercompany recharge booking, current and deferred tax on equity, and the equity footnote and local statutory disclosures, prepared once and reused.
You will own equity reporting data from Shareworks, our equity administration platform, through to the ledgers, while staying hands-on: preparing and reviewing close materials, owning your own accounts, and serving as the first escalation point for the judgment calls in your domain.
Share-based compensation (SBC) is one of the most cross-functional areas of our reporting.
Grants, vesting, exercises and the events that follow each carry requirements for US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP expense, pushdown and recharge postings, tax provisioning, payroll withholding, transfer pricing and statutory disclosure, and those needs are met across Equity Administration, Equity Reporting, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Transfer Pricing and Global Payroll from a single set of award-level records.
This is a build role: you will take the open workstreams from manual to automated, work with Finance Systems and Shareworks to build the reports each stage needs, finalize the policies and agreements that sit behind recharges, and bring the end-to-end process to a scalable, efficient and fully compliant close.
We are looking for someone who has owned equity accounting in a growing global organization before and wants to do it again at one of the most important companies in the world.
section_responsibilities:
Close ownership
Own the equity portfolio through month-end and quarter-end close: US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP equity expense, pushed down and booked by entity, including reconciliations, journal entries and variance commentary
Own intercompany recharge booking: invoicing, settlement, Treasury communication and the foreign exchange (FX) that follows
Own current and deferred tax on equity by entity and in local currency, including the IFRS deferred tax mark to the share price and windfalls or shortfalls through the tax provision
Ensure every close deliverable is audit-ready, with clear documentation of positions and supporting evidence
Technical accounting and policy
Write, own and maintain the accounting policies and standard operating procedures (SOPs) for equity across US GAAP, IFRS and local GAAP: grant-date fair value and expense schedules, recharge basis by entity, mobility apportionment, and the treatment of cancellations, modifications and one-off events
Partner closely with Tax to close every open policy position and execute the recharge agreements that depend on them
Research the tax and accounting rules for each new jurisdiction entered and categorize it under our framework before the first grant lands there
Own the equity footnote and local statutory disclosures for all entities, including the award rollforward for each period with internal transfers, and the external audit responses that support them
Controls
Design and operate Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) controls across equity expense, recharges and deferred tax; review control evidence and own timely remediation of any gaps
Establish completeness and cut-off controls so that the same award, the same entity, the same event dates and the same FX rate flow from Shareworks to every ledger, report and return
Systems and automation
Anticipate changes in reporting needs and work with Finance Systems and Shareworks to build them: IFRS expense and deferred tax reports in local currency at Workday rates, mobility snapshots driving expense apportionment, corporate tax apportionment rules, and exercise and disclosure reports with mobility detail
Automate the monthly pushdown and recharge postings and the reconciliation of deferred tax to expense reports, replacing manual work
Document workflows and controls in a way that supports knowledge transfer, audit evidence and scale
Cross-functional partnership
Partner with Equity Administration, Equity Reporting, Accounting, Treasury, Tax, Transfer Pricing and Global Payroll so each stage of an award is handled from every statutory and reporting perspective and every stakeholder has the data they need
Record in the local books (secondary ledgers) the local SBC expense and recharges that feed the cost base for transfer pricing
Translate complex equity accounting into plain language for non-finance stakeholders
Equity events
Lead the cross-functional, cross-jurisdictional review of one-off equity events such as tender offers and share repurchases, covering the accounting, the deduction, payroll withholding, Treasury and the resulting disclosures
Coordinate with Tax and advisers on open conclusions, such as the apportionment logic for corporation tax versus payroll tax, so report configurations are right before they are built, manual rework is minimized and the data serves every purpose it is built for

location: San Francisco, CA; New York City, NY
section_about:
The Claude Partner Network is how consulting firms, systems integrators, and other services partners build practices around Claude.
When a company chooses a partner, it wants to know which firms have done this work well, in its industry and for its use case.
Specializations are how the program will give it: credentials showing that a partner has demonstrated expertise in a given domain area.
As Partner Specializations Lead, you'll own this program end to end: the requirements a firm has to meet, the evidence review that decides who qualifies, the benefits that make a specialization worth earning, and the operating rhythm that keeps it credible year after year.
Your job is to take an early framework into a structure that scales: opening it to thousands of partners, running evaluation cycles, and launching new specializations with cross-functional input.
This role suits someone who likes owning a standard.
You'll work with partner managers, operations, enablement, marketing, and industry teams who each hold a piece of the program, and with senior leaders at partner firms who care a great deal about the outcome.
A specialization only means something if it's earned, so you'll need to be rigorous with evidence, consistent in your decisions, and firm and clear when the answer is no.
section_responsibilities:
Own each specialization's requirements, evidence standards, and benefits, and keep them current as our products and the partner network change
Run each evaluation cycle from invitation to decision: collect partner evidence, reconcile it against internal data, lead the review, and document every decision
Make and defend qualification decisions, including borderline cases, and apply the standard consistently across firms of very different sizes
Communicate outcomes to partner executives and their Anthropic account teams, including clear guidance for firms that did not qualify
Open the program to the wider partner network, and recommend which specializations come next based on customer demand, partner readiness, and Anthropic's priorities
Define the evidence standard for new specializations with Applied AI, Product, and industry go-to-market teams
Coordinate the teams that deliver the program's benefits (marketing, the partner directory, field enablement, technical support) so that earning a specialization leads to something real
Work with Partner Enablement so that partner learning paths and certifications support each specialization
Build the operating rhythm: renewal, remediation periods, an appeals path, and the tracking and reporting that show whether the program is working
Design the review process to scale, using Claude and automation so that routine steps don't depend on a person
Write and maintain partner-facing guidance (program guide sections, FAQs, application materials), clear enough for a partner to know where it stands without asking us, and internal guidance for field teams
Use program data to recommend where each requirement's bar should sit and when it should move, and bring those recommendations to partner leadership

In this unique company, technology, and moment in history, your work will be critical to informing our strategy as we deploy safe, frontier AI at scale to the world.
You'll be the senior data science leader embedded in our Core Apps product team and a strategic thought partner to its product leads.
You'll help set product direction for Claude Code and other new bets across Core Apps: bringing a point of view on where to invest, how to grow our Apps business, and how to deliver more value for our users.
As a tech lead manager, you'll also manage a small team of Product Data Scientists, setting their agenda and raising the bar for how data shapes product decisions.

location: New York City, NY
section_about:
As the leader of our Enterprise Asset & Wealth Management sales organization, you will build and lead a team that brings transformational AI to the world's leading asset managers, wealth managers, and private markets firms.
These are organizations rethinking how they generate investment insight, serve clients and advisors, scale personalization, and meet fiduciary and regulatory obligations.
They are looking for a partner they trust to take frontier AI from promising pilots into production at the core of their business.
You will own a broad portfolio of major AWM institutions at very different stages of AI adoption, from firms already running Claude in production to those just beginning their journey.
Your coverage will span global and regional asset managers, alternatives managers, and wealth businesses.
You will lead Account Executives, design the coverage and territory model, and build the repeatable, AWM-specific plays that turn early wins into durable, scaled adoption across research, portfolio and client operations, advisor productivity, and compliance and supervision.
The selling is technical and multi-stakeholder: platform decisions, model governance, security and procurement rigor, and solutions built on Claude through our API, Claude for Enterprise, Claude Code, and partner cloud platforms.
You will shape strategy and operating rhythm while staying personally engaged with executives on the pursuits that matter most.
This is a rare opportunity to build an organization, not just run a number: to shape how the asset and wealth management industry adopts frontier AI, and to do it at a company where safety, trust, and long-term customer outcomes are central to how we sell.

Define AWM go-to-market strategy and coverage design, including segmentation across asset managers, alternatives managers, and wealth platforms, territories, account prioritization, and vertical value propositions, and evolve the coverage model as the business scales

Orchestrate cross-functional and partner motions with Customer Success, Marketing, Partnerships, Legal, cloud partners, and the data and technology providers that AWM firms rely on, to deliver a seamless customer experience, and represent Anthropic with customers and at industry events as a visible, trusted leader

As the Sales Manager for Life Sciences at Anthropic, you'll lead the foundational team introducing our frontier AI platform to the pharma and biotech ecosystem, spanning large pharma, mid-size and emerging biotech, and the organizations that support drug development.
You'll build and develop a team of Strategic Account Executives who drive adoption of safe, frontier AI by securing strategic deals with pharmaceutical and biotech companies.
You'll bring deep domain fluency in how drugs are discovered, developed, approved, and launched to coach your team's consultative sales approach, while becoming a trusted advisor yourself to senior pharma and biotech stakeholders, helping them embed and deploy AI across the drug lifecycle from target discovery through commercialization.
In collaboration with Product and Marketing, you'll continuously refine the team's value proposition, sales methodology, and market positioning to resonate with decision-makers across large pharma and biotech.
The ideal candidate has a passion for developing new market segments within pharma and biotech, pinpointing high-potential opportunities across discovery, preclinical, clinical, regulatory, manufacturing, and commercial functions, and building a team that can execute strategies to capture them.
By driving deployment of Anthropic's emerging products across pharma and biotech organizations, you'll help them accelerate the path from science to patients while advancing the ethical development of AI.

Build and lead a specialized team of Strategic Account Executives covering large pharma and biotech accounts, setting growth targets by segment and coaching reps through the full sales cycle from outbound to close

Anthropic's compute runs on a growing global portfolio of data centers built with development partners.
As a Senior Field Engineer on the Data Center Design and Engineering team, you will work side by side with developers, general contractors and engineers of record to resolve technical issues on site and speed up construction.
You will spend most of your time on active sites, acting as our team's eyes, voice and technical judgment in the field.
You will spot problems first, get the right people moving, and stay with each issue until it is closed.
You don't need a data center background.
We care more about whether you have delivered complex industrial projects from the field and can get contractors and partners to act when you have no formal authority over them.
section_responsibilities:
Be our engineering presence on site.
You will walk installed work against the approved design and build working relationships with developers, general contractors, engineers of record, vendors and commissioning teams.
You will hold design acceptance on our team's behalf, deciding whether installed work meets the design.
When field conditions and drawings disagree, you will be the first call.
You will settle what you can on the spot and bring in the right discipline engineer for the rest.
More than 50% of your working time will be at project sites, often with overnight travel across multiple sites.
The rest will be remote from your home base.
Get issues closed.
You will keep one prioritized list of open engineering issues for your sites, each with an owner and a date.
You will follow up in person, challenge dates that don't hold up, and escalate early with a clear recommendation when something is stuck.
Find out why things fail.
When equipment, an installation or a test fails, you will gather the evidence, test the first explanation, and trace the failure to its underlying cause.
You will confirm that the fix works and check whether other sites carry the same risk.
Clear the path to commissioning and handover.
You will check the interfaces between power, cooling, controls and structure before they surface as test failures.
You will drive RFIs, deviations and field changes to decisions, so that open engineering questions don't hold up the crews.
Bring the field back into the design.
You will turn recurring site problems into changes to our designs, standards and audit checklists.
Each project should make the next one easier to deliver.

You won't manage construction crews or direct contractors' means and methods; those stay with our construction delivery partners.
You will work with our discipline engineers and hold the field view, rather than produce design documents.

location: San Francisco, CA
section_about:
As a Senior Software Engineer on the Life Sciences team, you'll build biology software that our own scientists and the wider research community can depend on, and you'll be one of the main people representing that work to computational biologists outside Anthropic.
The Life Sciences team works to accelerate progress in biology with AI, combining frontier models with hands-on computational and experimental research.
We want the tools, pipelines, datasets, and benchmarks we build in genomics and structural biology to be useful beyond our own projects, so we plan to release them to the community.
Computational biology has a long tradition of open, shared software, and we want to contribute to it well.
Every release should be something a researcher can install, run on their own data, and trust: correct on real inputs, validated against reference data and established methods, documented, versioned, and maintained after launch.
You'll own that standard.
You'll write a large share of the code yourself, decide when something is ready to ship, and stay with it once people start using it.
You'll also be an active member of the biology software community: maintaining public repositories, answering issues, speaking at conferences and workshops, and bringing what you hear from researchers back into what we build next.
We use Claude and AI coding agents heavily to build software, and we expect you to do the same across design, implementation, testing, and review.
Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand: you should understand it, test it, and measure its performance before it ships.
We're looking for someone with deep software engineering experience who already works this way.
The shape of the role is flexible.
You might spend most of your time as an individual contributor, or you might lead a small group of engineers and scientists while continuing to contribute directly.
Your focus can be genomics, structural biology, or both.
Experience in other areas of computational biology is welcome, and we expect the work to range more widely over time.
What matters most is a record of biology software that other people have adopted and relied on.
This is a chance to shape how AI is put to work in biological research, on problems that matter for human health and scientific understanding.
If building software that scientists trust is the work you want to do, we want to hear from you.

You'll own high-value engagements where we collaborate directly with customers to build and deploy agents into their most critical business processes.
This is a founding team: you will help us to build technical playbooks and define the processes and repeatable patterns needed for us to scale this emerging motion.
You will champion our mission in the field, ensure world class delivery, and bring insights back to our product and research teams on a regular basis.
You'll own engagements end-to-end, from SOW through production deployment.
You'll work alongside Forward Deployed Engineers who build the technical solution, while you own product scoping, stakeholder management, value measurement, and the organizational complexity that comes with deploying AI agents in enterprise environments.
You need to be technical enough to hold architecture conversations with engineering stakeholders and polished enough to run executive briefings with C-suite sponsors.
section_responsibilities:
Own the technical delivery plan for each engagement.
Structure SOWs with clear scope, milestones, dependencies, success criteria, and value hypotheses.
Translate customer business objectives into a sequenced roadmap that FDEs execute against.
Lead technical discovery: map customer workflows, identify constraints, define MVP scope, and shape the solution architecture for custom agent deployments.
Run day-to-day engineering execution and delivery across Anthropic and customer teams.
Keep progress unblocked and sequenced.
Make real-time trade-offs on scope and priority to protect the critical path.
Own product scoping for field engagements: define the MVP, author requirements documentation, prioritize the engineering backlog, and manage scope against success criteria as requirements evolve.
Own the customer relationship throughout delivery.
Lead executive briefings, manage stakeholder communications across technical leads and procurement, and represent Anthropic's technical credibility with senior business and engineering leaders.
Own value measurement and ROI: define impact hypotheses, set baselines and KPIs, run pre- and post-deployment measurement, and report outcomes to executive sponsors.
Codify reusable solution patterns, evaluation frameworks, and technical playbooks.
Extract what works across engagements and feed field signals back to Product and Research to improve our platform and models.
Navigate enterprise and regulatory complexity: security reviews, legal approvals, procurement processes, compliance requirements, and organizational dynamics.
Manage scope and change: handle evolving requirements, set expectations, negotiate contract modifications, identify risks early, and escalate with clear context when needed.
Run delivery operations: sprint ceremonies, milestone reviews, and progress reporting.
Travel to customer sites to build relationships, unblock delivery, and accelerate adoption (25-50% expected).
section_requirements:
Have 5+ years of customer-facing technical delivery leadership - this could be technical engagement management, technical program management, or technical product management, founders/startups, technical-adjacent backgrounds, professional services, consulting, or enterprise software.
Have delivered AI, ML, or LLM-based agentic solutions into production.
You understand solution patterns, integration approaches, and what breaks in real environments.
Can lead architecture discussions with engineering stakeholders, evaluate technical trade-offs, and pressure-test technical decisions.
You won't write production code, but you will own the technical direction of engagements alongside FDEs.
Have a track record delivering complex, high-stakes technical projects for enterprise clients where outcomes depended on tight coordination and fast decision-making, ideally across multiple workstreams in regulated industries.
Have executive presence - polished, credible, and comfortable representing Anthropic to senior leaders in high-stakes environments.
Thrive in ambiguity and bring structure where none exists.
Have a builder's mindset - you're here to create a function, not join one.
section_preferred:
Experience in financial services, healthcare/life sciences, or pharmaceutical verticals.
Background at a Forward Deployed Engineering company or professional services and consulting firms.
Exceptional understanding of LLM capabilities and limitations.
Experience with regulated industries and compliance requirements.
Experience managing delivery teams with embedded engineers at customer sites.
Familiarity with AI agent frameworks, tool use patterns, and orchestration architectures.

section_about:
Anthropic is looking for a Contracts Manager to support our commercial and technology transactions.
You'll partner with our GTM teams on enterprise customer deals, including some of our largest and most complex agreements.
You'll review, draft, and negotiate commercial and procurement contracts that support our AI systems, and build the contracting processes that help us scale.
You'll collaborate with Product, Sales, Finance, Business Operations, Research, and Procurement.

We'd love to hear where else you'd be interested in pitching in, whether because of your experience or your interests.

section_about:
Claude Frontier Academy is where organizations nominate their strongest people to build deep, hands-on skills with Claude.
Backed by a $100 million commitment, Anthropic aims to train 10,000 Frontier Deployed Engineers by the end of 2027.
The Academy's first program, the Frontier Deployed Engineer (FDE) Residency, brings engineers from leading customers and partners together in cohorts, and more programs will follow.
We're looking for a Marketing Lead to make the Academy a name the market knows and a credential people are proud to earn.
As the Academy's first dedicated marketer, you'll own how it shows up in the world.
You're a creative, versatile marketer who thinks in terms of brand and communications and also knows how to position, launch, and grow programs.
You'll turn each program launch into a major market moment, celebrate milestones like new cohorts and the first badges earned, and build a community of graduates who help tell the story.
Because the Academy serves both partners and customers, this role will sit on our Partner Marketing team.
You'll work directly with partners and customers to secure their participation in announcements and bring them into our launch and amplification plans.
You'll help shape the Academy's strategy and annual plan and represent marketing with senior leaders, while staying hands-on enough to write the first draft yourself.
Partners and customers already engage with other Anthropic education and training programs, so you'll be thoughtful about how the Academy fits alongside them.
If you've built a branded program at a B2B technology company and want to do it again at a much bigger scale, this role is for you.
section_responsibilities:
Own the marketing strategy and annual plan for Claude Frontier Academy and its programs, working with Academy leadership to set priorities and goals
Build and maintain a calendar of market moments for the Academy and each program, including program launches, new cohorts, and badge milestones
Lead launches end to end, from messaging and announcement drafts through legal and executive review, launch-day execution and post-launch amplification
Partner with Communications on press releases and announcements, including sourcing customer and partner quotes and securing approval to use their names
Align early with Partnerships, Communications, and Account Teams on which customers and partners are named in each announcement, who gets a heads-up before it goes live, and how to answer those who aren't named
Develop amplification plans with partners and customers across social posts, blogs, newsletters, and their own announcements, and turn cohort results into joint customer and partner stories
Grow the Academy's presence on LinkedIn and other social channels with content that showcases programs, cohorts, and graduates
Own the Academy's web presence and any paid promotion, working with our web team and with creative and agency partners
Build a community program that keeps cohort members and badge holders connected and turns them into advocates for the Academy
Work with Brand to extend the Academy's naming and brand architecture as new programs launch, keeping it consistent with, and clearly distinct from, Anthropic's other education and training offerings
Learn Anthropic's other education and training programs, such as Claude Academy, Claude certifications, and Partner Basecamp, and work with their teams to define where Claude Frontier Academy fits, where the programs connect, and how they reference each other, so partners and customers see one clear path
Equip Account Teams and Partner Account Managers with FAQs, internal announcements, and guidance so they can answer questions, help customers and partners register their interest, and set clear expectations on participation
Keep senior stakeholders aligned through regular status updates and clear recommendations, and define and report on success metrics for Academy marketing

location: Boston, MA
section_about:
Anthropic's Life Sciences team is building a world-class research group focused on making fundamental biological discoveries.
The team combines cutting-edge AI with hands-on biological research, positioning Anthropic at the forefront of AI-accelerated scientific discovery.
We are hiring a Research Operations Lead to be the operational backbone of our team: the person who makes sure scientists can walk in every morning and get straight to science.
You'll take on the operational systems we've started - procurement, inventory, safety, equipment, space - make them better, and scale them as the lab and its needs grow.
We're hiring for trajectory as much as for what you've already done: the scope of this role will grow with the size of the team, and we want someone who's excited by that.
This role is a rare opportunity to build the operational foundation of Anthropic's biology team and to grow with it.
The systems you put in place will shape how a frontier AI company does experimental biology for years to come.
If you're energized by high-ownership operational work in the service of ambitious science, we'd love to hear from you.

Build on and extend the operational systems a growing group needs: procurement workflows, inventory and sample tracking, equipment maintenance and calibration schedules, onboarding and training, SOPs
Manage facilities and space: coordinate buildouts, moves, and equipment installs; act as the primary interface to building management, contractors, and Anthropic's central Workplace and IT teams
Own the operating budget: track spend against plan, run the capital equipment purchasing process, and partner with Finance on forecasting and reporting
Manage vendor and supplier relationships: including contract research organizations: source and qualify vendors, negotiate quotes and service contracts, schedule preventive maintenance and field-service visits, and hold suppliers to their commitments

location: San Francisco, CA; New York City, NY
section_about:
As the Content Strategy Lead for Executive Programs, you will own what Anthropic brings to the table when we sit down with senior leaders from our most strategic customers.
That covers Executive Briefings, Customer Advisory Boards, Executive Councils, and the other small-room gatherings where a C-level audience meets with our leaders, product teams, and researchers.
You will set the content strategy across these programs, build the library of modules and the bench of speakers, and lead the team that keeps our content fresh as our models and products evolve.
This role works cross-functionally with Product & Solutions Marketing, who owns positioning and messaging across industries and products, and customer programs which owns each program's operations, intake, and customer experience.
You own the layer in between: turning Anthropic's product, research, and policy story into sessions built for an executive audience, deciding who is best placed to deliver them, and designing interactive formats and demos that work for customers building on the frontier.
The right candidate has a product marketing or narrative background, has built content for C-level customer audiences at an enterprise technology company, and has managed a team.
section_responsibilities:
Set and execute the content strategy across Executive Briefings, Customer Advisory Boards, Executive Councils, and other gatherings of strategic customers: the themes for the year, the narrative that connects them, and how content differs by program, audience, and purpose.
Build and maintain an evergreen library of content modules that program leads and account teams can assemble into an agenda without starting from scratch.
Modules span product and roadmap, research, safety and policy, industry and use-case sessions, demos, and discussion guides.
Keep the library current.
Set a refresh cadence tied to model and product launches, retire what is stale, maintain a pipeline of net-new content modules, and make sure nothing in front of a customer executive is out of date.
Identify, recruit, develop and certify speakers from Anthropic's executive, product, research, and go-to-market teams.
Maintain the cross-program roster, shape each speaker's session, and prepare them for the room.
Design the experience, not only the presentation.
Choose the format that fits the audience and the goal, whether that is a working session, a live demo, a conversation with a researcher, or a peer discussion among customers.
Partner with program leads on agendas for the highest-priority engagements, tailoring modules to the customer's objectives.
Set the standards and templates that let every other engagement meet the same bar.
Work with Product & Solutions Marketing, Product, and Research so that executive-level content is ready when a launch happens, not weeks after.
Capture what customers say in these rooms, including themes, objections, and requests.
Route it to Product, Research, Marketing, and go-to-market leadership, and use it to improve the content.
Measure what works, including session feedback, module usage, and speaker performance, and work with program leads to connect content to program outcomes.
Hire, manage, and develop the team responsible for executive program content, and set its quality bar.
Use Claude to scale the work: build workflows that tailor modules to a customer's industry and priorities so a customized session does not require a rebuild.
section_requirements:
Built content for C-level customer audiences in executive briefings, advisory boards, executive councils, or similar programs.
Built a content system that other people rely on, such as a module library, a session catalog, or a speaker program, and kept it current through frequent product change.
The technical fluency to work directly with researchers and engineers, understand what they have built, and explain it accurately to a business executive.
Experience coaching senior executives and technical experts as speakers, including giving direct feedback on their material.
Judgment about format: you know when a room needs a presentation, a demo, or a facilitated discussion, and you can design each one.
Experience managing people, including hiring and developing a team.
A high bar for writing.
You can draft an executive session narrative yourself and improve one written by someone else.
Genuine interest in AI and in helping the world's largest enterprises adopt it responsibly.
section_preferred:
12+ years in product marketing, executive content, or executive customer programs at a B2B technology company.
You have owned positioning and messaging for a technical product and know how to adapt it for different audiences.
Experience at a company where the product changes quickly and content has a short shelf life.

job_title: Data Center Power Generation and Microgrids Engineer
location: Remote-Friendly, United States
section_about:
Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle.
The loads involved are large enough - and arrive fast enough - that utility supply alone often can't meet the need on the timeline required, and the step-load behavior of large accelerator clusters creates power-quality and ride-through demands that conventional backup-generation designs weren't built for.
Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for solving that problem: delivering facilities that can be energized early, ride through grid disturbances, and present a well-behaved load at the point of interconnection (POI).
As a Data Center Power Generation & Microgrids Engineer, you'll own the behind-the-meter generation and storage architecture for Anthropic's data center portfolio.
That means the on-site generation fleet - reciprocating engine gensets, gas turbines, fuel cells - and the battery energy storage systems that buffer load steps and provide ride-through.
It means the microgrid layer that ties them together: islanding and resynchronization, black-start, load-shedding, and generation dispatch.
And it means the grid side: interconnection studies and agreements, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and power quality at the point of interconnection.
You'll also own our temporary- and bridging-generation strategies - the plans that let a site energize and start serving load before permanent utility service is available, and transition cleanly once it is.
This is a deeply cross-functional role.
You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team on where and how generation and storage tie into the site electrical distribution, controls, and SCADA, and with our hardware and compute teams to understand the load characteristics you're designing against.
You'll be Anthropic's technical counterpart to on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, utilities, and ISOs/RTOs.
Expect roughly 20-35% travel for design reviews, factory witness testing, and site startup.
section_responsibilities:
On-site generation engineering
Own Anthropic's behind-the-meter generation architecture across the portfolio - prime-mover selection and sizing (reciprocating engines, gas turbines, fuel cells), paralleling topology, redundancy, fuel systems, and emissions controls - and maintain the generation basis of design and technical specifications that build partners and generation providers design against
Set the day-one vs. day-N plant sizing and expansion strategy - what the plant needs on day one so it can be expanded or augmented later, and how to add units, storage, or a grid tie to a system already running
Characterize the data center load for external generation partners - step changes, ramps, oscillation, fault behavior, and non-IT load - so providers can size and tune their plant against the real duty
Model generation response against the load profile of large-scale ML training - step-load acceptance, block loading, transient frequency and voltage response, load rejection - and set the acceptance criteria (e.g., per ISO 8528-5) that generation packages are tested against
Develop temporary- and bridging-generation strategies that deliver early site energization ahead of permanent utility service, including the sequencing, protection, and controls changes needed to transition from temporary to permanent power without stranding equipment or capacity
Ensure generation designs meet NFPA 37, NFPA 110 where the plant provides emergency or legally required standby power, fuel-gas and fuel-storage codes (e.g., NFPA 54, NFPA 30), and applicable emissions requirements, and coordinate with environmental and permitting counterparts on the technical inputs to air permits
Energy storage & microgrid architecture
Size and specify battery energy storage systems for ride-through, step-load buffering, and power-quality support - including cell chemistry and enclosure selection, inverter selection (grid-forming vs. grid-following), UL 9540 listing, UL 9540A large-scale fire test data, and NFPA 855 installation requirements - and own the thermal and fire-protection interfaces
Define the site microgrid topology and operating modes - grid-parallel, islanded, and black-start - and the transition logic between them, including load-shedding schemes, resynchronization criteria, and the conditions under which the site separates from and reconnects to the utility
Specify the functional requirements for the microgrid controller - generation dispatch, set-point coordination across rotating and inverter-based sources, mode management - and drive its implementation, testing, and integration into site SCADA and the electrical power monitoring system (EPMS)
Help define the protection and control requirements for generation and storage sources so that interconnection protection, anti-islanding, and source-transfer schemes are consistent from the generator terminals through the point of interconnection
Grid interconnection & power quality
Lead the technical side of utility interconnection for sites with on-site generation or storage - interconnection applications, studies, and agreements, ISO/RTO processes, IEEE 1547/2800 compliance, and interconnection protection
Own power quality at the point of interconnection - flicker per IEEE 1453, harmonics per IEEE 519, voltage regulation, reactive-power and power-factor requirements - and design the generation, storage, and filtering mitigations needed to keep the site within its interconnection limits under real training-load behavior
Run or critically review the power-system studies that support interconnection and microgrid design - load flow, short-circuit contribution from rotating and inverter-based sources, transient stability, motor-starting and step-load studies, and electromagnetic-transient studies where inverter controls matter
Vendor diligence & delivery
Lead technical due diligence on on-site generation providers, BESS integrators, and microgrid-controller vendors - evaluating equipment and controls on engineering merit, stress-testing performance and availability guarantees, and reviewing proposed architectures against Anthropic's basis of design
Define the technical performance terms in energy-services agreements with on-site generation providers - availability, power quality, ramp, and ride-through, each with a definition, meter, test protocol, and acceptance criteria - working with energy commercial and legal counterparts
Review and disposition design packages, submittals, shop drawings, and deviation requests from generation providers and their EPCs, and hold partners to Anthropic's reliability and maintainability requirements
Support commissioning of generation, storage, and microgrid systems - witnessing factory and site acceptance tests, defining and observing integrated systems tests (islanding, resynchronization, black-start, load-step), and resolving field issues against design intent
Manage concurrent generation and microgrid scopes across multiple sites, and contribute to the continuous improvement of Anthropic's generation and interconnection design standards as the portfolio and the technology both evolve

job_title: Data Center Substation, Protection & Automation Engineer
location: Remote-Friendly, United States
section_about:
Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle.
Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure - partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and utilities to stand up facilities that can reliably power some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry.
At the scale we build, our campuses are typically served by dedicated high-voltage substations and a medium-voltage distribution network that may also integrate on-site generation and battery energy storage - and the protection, control, and automation layer is what keeps all of it selective, coordinated, and observable.
As a Data Center Substation, Protection & Automation Engineer, you'll own the protection and automation architecture across Anthropic's US portfolio - from the utility point of interconnection (POI) through the HV/MV substation, the MV distribution loop, and down into LV switchgear.
You'll develop and maintain our protection philosophy and reference relay settings, run and review the short-circuit, coordination, and arc-flash studies that underpin them, design the substation automation and SCADA architecture, and define how relays and meters integrate into the electrical power monitoring system (EPMS) - giving operators real-time visibility and sequence-of-events data when something trips.
You'll also be our technical lead on the protection side of utility interconnection - working relay settings, transfer-trip, and ride-through requirements with transmission owners and ISOs/RTOs.
Protection engineering and substation automation are the core of this role; substation physical design is a strong plus but not a prerequisite - we'd like to hear from protection and P&C engineers who have spent their careers on relays, schemes, and studies even if they haven't owned a substation general arrangement.
You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team, our build partners' A/E firms, relay and switchgear vendors, and utility protection groups.
Expect roughly 20-35% travel for witnessing factory acceptance and relay testing, and supporting site energization and commissioning.
section_responsibilities:
Protection engineering
Own Anthropic's protection philosophy and basis of design across the electrical system - HV substation, MV distribution, generator and energy-storage interties, and LV switchgear - and maintain the reference relay settings and protection one-line templates our build partners design against
Specify protective relays and develop relay settings for transformer, feeder, bus, generator, motor, and arc-flash protection applications, working across major platforms (e.g., SEL, GE Multilin, ABB, Siemens, Schneider)
Perform and critically review short-circuit, protective-device coordination, and arc-flash studies; use findings to steer equipment selection, settings, and incident-energy mitigation
Implement automatic transfer, load-shed, and restoration schemes in protection and automation logic, and make sure they stay secure and coordinated under every credible contingency
Review protection and control design packages, relay settings calculations, and coordination studies from build partners and A/E firms against our basis of design, and drive closure on deviations and exceptions
Substation automation & SCADA
Design the substation automation architecture for each site - IEC 61850 station and process bus, GOOSE messaging, RTUs/gateways, local HMI, sequence-of-events recording, and time synchronization - and drive standardization of that architecture across the portfolio
Integrate protective relays, meters, and switchgear controls into the electrical power monitoring system (EPMS) and substation SCADA; define electrical points lists and event/waveform capture, applying the site alarm and HMI standards
Help define the network topology, redundancy, and cybersecurity boundaries between substation automation, EPMS, and the facility BMS/DCIM layer, and how protection events surface to operations
Evaluate and qualify relay, RTU, gateway, and EPMS platforms on technical merit, and work with supply chain to build a diversified vendor base that mitigates lead-time and single-source risk
Substation design & utility interface
Review HV/MV substation design packages from build partners - single-line and three-line diagrams, bus configuration, general arrangement, equipment specifications, grounding-grid design, and control-building layout - and confirm the protection and control design is buildable and maintainable
Work with local utilities, transmission owners, and ISOs/RTOs on interconnection protection requirements - relay settings submittals, transfer-trip and communications-assisted schemes, POI study review, and protection settings that satisfy ride-through and grid-code requirements
Review the protection and control interface for on-site generation and battery energy storage interconnections, including anti-islanding, synchronizing, and intertie protection
Support NERC PRC compliance for applicable facilities - settings documentation, misoperation analysis, and periodic maintenance and testing basis
Testing, commissioning & standards
Develop relay test plans and factory and site acceptance test procedures for protection and automation systems, and witness FAT, relay secondary-injection testing, GOOSE messaging and end-to-end scheme testing, and integrated systems testing
Review the protection and control steps of energization and switching methods of procedure (MOPs), support first-energization of substations and MV distribution, and resolve protection and control issues found in the field
Lead root-cause analysis of protection operations and misoperations using relay event records, sequence-of-events data, and disturbance records, and feed findings back into settings and standards
Build and continuously improve Anthropic's internal protection and automation standards - settings templates, scheme logic libraries, test procedures, and commissioning checklists - so each new site starts from a proven baseline

section_about:
Training and serving frontier AI models requires compute infrastructure at a scale and density that pushes past what conventional data center designs were built to handle.
Anthropic's Data Center Infrastructure team is responsible for delivering that physical infrastructure - partnering with build partners, equipment manufacturers, and utilities to stand up facilities that can reliably power some of the largest accelerator clusters in the industry.
As a Data Center Electrical Engineer - Design, you'll own the electrical architecture of our facilities from the utility service entrance through to the rack - substation interface, medium- and high-voltage distribution, on-site generation and storage integration, UPS, switchgear, busway, and rack power.
You'll develop and maintain the basis of design, reference architectures, and technical specifications that our build partners and A/E firms design against, and you'll be the point of technical authority when their drawings and calculations come back for review.
You'll run the engineering studies - short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, load flow, and power quality - and you'll keep the architecture ahead of rapidly increasing rack densities and the unique load characteristics of large-scale ML training.
A central part of this role is speed-to-capacity through prefabrication: you'll shape Anthropic's offsite-manufactured electrical strategy - modular skids, e-houses, and prefabricated power assemblies - and drive its standardization across sites.
You'll work closely with colleagues across the infrastructure team, with our hardware and compute teams to translate accelerator requirements into electrical design criteria, and with supply chain to qualify and diversify regional equipment vendors.
Expect roughly 10-25% travel for design reviews, partner and vendor meetings, factory witness testing, and site visits to support commissioning and startup.
section_responsibilities:
Electrical design & engineering
Lead the electrical design of critical data center infrastructure across the US portfolio, including the utility interface and substation, site medium- and high-voltage distribution, generators, UPS, switchgear, transformers, busway, and grounding
Develop and maintain Anthropic's electrical basis of design, reference architectures, and technical specifications for critical power distribution - covering switchgear, UPS systems, PDUs, busway, and rack power delivery - producing designs that meet our reliability and maintainability requirements while staying within budgetary targets
Perform and validate engineering studies - including short-circuit, protection coordination, arc flash, load flow, and power quality analysis - and use the findings to steer topology, redundancy, equipment-selection, and protection-setting decisions
Design and plan data center hall power distribution layouts for newly allocated spaces in coordination with the telecom, mechanical and cooling design
Prefabrication & modular delivery
Drive Anthropic's prefabricated and modular electrical strategy - developing modular skids, e-houses, and prefabricated power assemblies, and partnering with external engineering and manufacturing teams on a productization roadmap that accelerates deployment and reduces onsite labor
Design for offsite manufacture and onsite assembly: define the interfaces between prefabricated components and site-built work, and the electrical interfaces and switchover points for temporary-to-permanent power sequencing
Drive standardization of modular electrical designs across sites to compress deployment timelines while preserving flexibility for site-specific constraints and evolving hardware generations
Partner, vendor & utility coordination
Work with regional vendors and manufacturers to specify and qualify major electrical equipment, and partner with supply chain to build a diversified vendor base that mitigates lead-time and single-source risk
Work with utilities and interconnection/transmission operators (e.g., ISOs/RTOs) to define site utility service and interconnection requirements, and with local authorities having jurisdiction to ensure designs comply with the National Electrical Code (NFPA 70/NEC), NFPA, IEEE, UL/ANSI, and local requirements
Work with Anthropic's hardware and compute teams to translate accelerator power, density, and power-quality requirements into electrical design criteria, and keep the reference architecture aligned with upcoming hardware generations
Present findings and design positions to internal stakeholders, build partners, and operations teams through clear reports and presentations, and defend them under challenge
Design review & quality
Review and approve electrical design packages, calculations, submittals, and shop drawings from build partners and MEP consultants; track clarifications, deviations, and exceptions against the basis of design, and hold the line on capacity, reliability, maintainability, and safety requirements
Perform technical due diligence and design reviews on data center developer and partner projects - evaluating their electrical single-lines, equipment selections, studies, and specifications against Anthropic's reliability, maintainability, and capacity requirements
Define project electrical scope and serve as the design authority on RFIs and field changes that affect design intent during procurement and construction
Support factory acceptance testing, commissioning, and startup - reviewing test procedures and results against design intent, participating on site for key milestones, and closing as-built changes back into the reference design
Manage concurrent projects across multiple geographies
Continuously improve Anthropic's internal electrical design standards, tooling, and delivery practices, and act as a technical leader within the engineering group and across the internal and external teams that support our data centers

section_about:

You will partner closely with engineering, demand planning, construction, and third parties to drive equipment availability, establish vendor relationships, and negotiate commercial agreements.
