job_title: Incident Management Lead, Data Center Security
location: United States: San Francisco; United States: Seattle; United States: New York; United States: Remote
section_about:
Anthropic operates and is building data center campuses around the world, run day to day through operating partners, site vendors, and contracted security services.
Things go wrong at those sites the way they go wrong at any critical infrastructure: access issues, contractor incidents, protests, weather, equipment failures, and occasionally something with the potential for global impact.
Today, what counts as an incident, who gets told, and how it is reported vary by site and by vendor.
As Lead for Crisis and Incident Management, you will build the program that removes that variance, and you will build it with the people who have to live with it.
The first job is definition: working with operating partners, site security vendors, managed-service providers, and internal teams to agree on what counts as a minor escalation versus a major incident of global impact, the severity levels in between, the thresholds that move an event from one level to the next, and who gets told, how fast, and in what format.
The second job is adoption: turning those definitions into playbooks, training, and exercises so that responders at every site and vendor actually respond the right way, and running the after-action reviews that show where they did not.
The third job is measurement: defining the incident metrics, building the reporting, and giving leadership a regular, accurate picture of how response is performing across the fleet.
Underneath all three sits the cross-functional work of getting partners to buy in, because a framework no partner has signed up to is a document, not a program.
Continuous coverage is part of the picture.
As the program matures, you will shape a 24/7 monitoring and response capability through GSOC-type managed services and site vendors, so that the framework holds at three in the morning at any site in the fleet.
That build-out follows from the definitions and partner agreements above rather than replacing them.
When a major incident does happen, you run it: activation, coordination, leadership communication, stand-down, and the after-action review that makes the program better.
This is a program-building role, not a shift-supervision role.
The deliverable is a framework that partners have adopted, that works at any site, and that reports on itself, run largely through vendors and managed services rather than a large in-house team.
Where existing processes and vendor arrangements don't support that, you will have the authority, and the expectation, to change them.
Role boundaries.
This seat is distinct from the Data Center Security Delivery Lead (who owns security through construction, commissioning, and handover on new builds), from regional security operations leads (who own steady-state regional programs and vendor relationships site by site), and from the team's systems-engineering roles (who build platforms and tooling).
This role owns the horizontal incident and crisis layer across the operating fleet: the incident definitions and severity framework, partner adoption and governance, incident reporting and metrics, major incident command, post-incident review, and, as it develops, the 24/7 coverage model, applied consistently across every site and vendor.
section_responsibilities:
You will build and own the global crisis and incident management program for data center physical security.
Incident definition and severity framework: define, with partners, what counts as an incident and the tiers from minor site escalation to major incident of global impact, with clear thresholds, escalation and activation criteria, notification requirements, and decision rights at each tier.
This is the foundation the rest of the program is built on.
Cross-functional partner buy-in and governance: bring operating partners, site security vendors, managed-service providers, and internal teams into the definition work so the framework is theirs as well as ours, and establish the governance (owners, review cadence, change process) that keeps it current as the fleet grows.
Adoption and response readiness: turn the framework into playbooks, training, and tabletop and functional exercises across sites and vendors, so responders know the right response before the next real incident and the escalation chain is tested by design.
Metrics and reporting: define the incident metrics that show whether definitions are being applied and whether response is improving, build the dashboards and reporting behind them, and own the executive reporting cadence, from real-time notification through leadership escalation and executive summaries.
Vendor and managed-service consistency: hold multiple vendors and GSOC-type providers to one standard: common definitions, common procedures, common reporting formats, common escalation triggers, with performance measured and enforced.
Major incident management: run the crisis process when an incident has multi-site or global impact: activation, coordination across sites, vendors, and internal teams, decision support to leadership, and formal stand-down.
Post-incident review and improvement: run structured after-action reviews, track corrective actions to closure, and feed lessons back into definitions, playbooks, procedures, and vendor contracts.
24/7 coverage model: as the program matures, design and run an always-on monitoring, escalation, and response capability through GSOC-type managed services and site security vendors, achieving continuous coverage without building a large in-house shift operation.
section_requirements:

Have driven adoption: you have taken a framework from paper into playbooks, training, and exercises, and can point to responders behaving differently as a result.

Work through influence across sites, vendors, and internal teams you don't control; you shape response rather than waiting to be given authority.

section_about:
Anthropic runs on a home-grown internal employee collaboration platform, that Ants use every day to plan, coordinate, and get work done alongside Claude.
Today it is a widely used tool.
We want it to become the centerpiece of how Anthropic works: the surface where people, teams, and Claude agents collaborate, and a living demonstration of what an AI-native company looks like from the inside.
You will be the first dedicated Product Manager for this platform, paired with a dedicated engineering team.
You will own the product end to end: the vision for where it goes, the roadmap that gets it there, and the outcomes that prove it worked.
The scope is company-wide, every employee is your customer, and the platform's success is a company-level goal, not a team-level one.
"And more" is deliberate.
As the platform matures, we expect it to inform how Anthropic shows enterprise customers what internal Claude adoption can look like, and potentially to shape external products.
You will help decide where that line sits.
section_responsibilities:
Set direction and drive a company-wide outcome
Define the product vision and a 3-6 month strategy for making the platform the default home for cross-functional collaboration at Anthropic, and get alignment from leadership across Security/IT, Engineering, Research, and G&A.
Own adoption, engagement, and satisfaction outcomes at the company level.
Set the metrics, instrument them, and be accountable for moving them with clear attribution.
Prioritize ruthlessly against a demand signal that will always exceed capacity; say no well and explain why.
Ship, fast and with craft
Lead a dedicated engineering team from discovery through launch.
Write the specs, make the calls, and keep velocity high without drama or burnout.
Set and hold the quality bar.
The platform should feel like a product Anthropic would be proud to ship externally, not an internal tool people tolerate.
Drive multiple workstreams in parallel core collaboration primitives, Claude-agent integration, integrations with the rest of the internal stack (Slack, Google Workspace, Claude Support, and others).
Build AGI-first
Design for where models will be in 3,6,12 months, not where they are today.
Assume Claude is a participant in collaboration, not a feature bolted onto it.
Partner closely with Research, Labs, and product teams on the Claude side so internal and external product thinking reinforce each other.
Own the safety, privacy, and data-handling tradeoffs inherent in a platform that touches company-wide information.
Make the hard calls; don't defer them upward.
Stay close to the customer
Build a systematic understanding of how different Ants and teams actually work: engineers, researchers, GTM, G&A, leadership.
Let that voice shape strategy, not just individual features.
Run regular discovery, dogfooding, and feedback loops; nothing about a launch should surprise you afterward.
Elevate the org
Establish PM craft inside Business Technology, a group that has strong engineers and operators but has not had product management before you.
Create the artifacts, rituals, and standards others reuse.
Uplevel cross-functional partners: help engineering, IT, and business stakeholders think in outcomes and customer problems.
Contribute to PM hiring and help attract talent to Anthropic.
What we're looking for
We hire on demonstrated impact - what you have shipped and moved - not on scope owned, team size, or tenure.
Impact
A track record of outcomes that affected a company-wide goal, with clear attribution to you, ideally on a platform, productivity, or collaboration product with a large user base (internal or external).
You create clarity in chaos: you are the person people go to when no one knows what to do, and you relentlessly find the right answer rather than the assigned one.
Velocity is a signature.
You have driven a company-wide initiative to completion, and you can juggle several at once one goal that took all your capacity is not enough at this level.
High craft is evident in what you ship; quality issues don't keep surfacing after launch.
Judgment
You build for frontier AI.
You have shipped products that leverage new model capabilities and you design for where capabilities are going, not just where they are.
Others learn to build AGI-first by watching you.
You are trusted to navigate difficult safety, privacy, and data tradeoffs, and you have slowed down or changed course for safety reasons before.
Deep, systematic customer understanding.
Customer voice shapes your strategy, and you are trusted on user tradeoffs.
Leadership
You improve PM craft as a whole, not just your own output, and you uplevel the cross-functional people around you.
People inside and outside product credit growth to you.
Knowledge you create becomes org capability rather than staying in your head.
You operate on behalf of the company, not your team.

Experience building or scaling collaboration, workflow, or productivity platforms (e.g., internal tools at scale, workplace/collaboration SaaS, developer or knowledge platforms).
Comfort operating inside an IT/Security org and partnering with engineering-heavy stakeholders.
Product background that spans consumer-grade polish and enterprise-grade constraints (identity, permissions, data classification, auditability).
Hands-on with Claude or other frontier models in building products, not just using them.
Why this role
Genuine whitespace.
First PM on the platform, first PM in Business Technology, dedicated engineering team, executive attention.
A customer you can reach.
Every user is a colleague.
Discovery is a Slack message away, and feedback loops are measured in hours.
Frontier leverage.
You get to build a collaboration product where Claude is a first-class participant, at the company building Claude.
Impact beyond the walls.
What you build becomes part of how Anthropic tells the story of an AI-native company to enterprise customers.

As the Global Supply Manager for Contract Manufacturing within the Data Center Infrastructure organization, you will own Anthropic's relationship with the contract manufacturers and ODMs that build our servers, racks, and accelerator systems.
Your ownership extends to both sides of this relationship: the commercial framing, structuring the agreements, pricing, and SLAs that define what the partner owes us, and the execution against it, sharing forecasts, scheduling build plans, and holding the partner to volume, on-time output, and inventory commitments.
This is not the sort of role where work stops after negotiation; the person who helps structure the deal is the same person accountable for the partner delivering against it every week.
You will work daily with our product and manufacturing engineers who support our partner sites, and with supply chain, finance, and deployment teams internally.
If you have owned a CM or ODM relationship through both a negotiation cycle and a production ramp, are passionate about HPC data centers, & enjoy working in complex, fast-paced environments, we welcome you to apply.
This is a hands-on role with up to 50% travel to partner factories in the US and abroad.
You should be as comfortable meeting with partners face to face as you are presenting a long term partner strategy to leadership.
Responsibilities Include:
Help structure and negotiate the CM/ODM commercial agreements, including MSAs, SOWs, pricing and NRE models, and liability and flexibility terms, with clear, measurable performance obligations.
Design the SLA/SLO framework and vendor scorecard for the manufacturing relationship, and oversee the governance cadence, from weekly operating reviews to QBRs with partner executives.
Share demand forecasts with the partner on a defined cadence and convert them into committed, capacity build plans aligned to our deployment schedule.
Ensure builds are scheduled against deployment need dates and hold the partner to committed volumes and on time output, driving recovery plans when production falls behind.
Ensure the partner maintains adequate materials and buffer inventory on site to protect the build plan and manage inventory risks against the forecast.
Verify partner billing against contracted rates, actual output, and approved NRE, and resolve discrepancies before invoices are approved.
Escalate performance issues through the partner's management chain with data, and own corrective actions through closure.
Coordinate with product engineering, manufacturing engineering, supply chain, and deployment operations so factory commitments and downstream plans stay aligned.

job_title: Environmental Health & Safety Manager, Data Center Construction and Operations
location: United States: Remote
section_about:
Anthropic is hiring an EHS Manager, Data Center Construction and Operations to own environment, health, and safety across the full lifecycle of our data center sites - from construction and commissioning through to live operations.
As we scale the physical infrastructure behind our research, this role makes sure the high-hazard work of building and running data centers is done safely, by our partners and for our people.
This is a specialized, field-facing, program-ownership role, and contractor safety is at the center of it.
Most of the hands-on work at these sites is performed by general contractors, subcontractors, and specialty trades, so your impact comes through how well you set expectations, qualify and oversee those partners, and hold multi-employer worksites to our safety standards.
You'll be Anthropic's safety presence on the ground - through active construction, the transition of commissioning, and the shift into operational EHS once a site is live.
You'll own these programs end to end today, and as our data center footprint grows you may build and lead a team to support them.
You won't be doing this alone: you'll partner closely with the EHS Lead - who will help you stand up the vendor, consultant, and specialist support you'll rely on - and work with our construction, infrastructure, operations, Security, and Legal partners, as well as the contractor and operator organizations running the sites.
section_responsibilities:
Contractor safety is the core of this role.
You'll build and run the programs that govern how contractors work on our sites - prequalification and selection, safety plan and method-statement review, site-specific orientation, high-hazard work permitting, and the audits and inspections that verify the work matches the plan.
On multi-employer worksites you'll set clear expectations, coordinate across general contractors and subcontractors, and hold every party accountable for working safely.
You'll own EHS across the construction, commissioning, and operations phases.
During construction that means the high-hazard exposures data centers involve - electrical and energized systems, working at height, heavy equipment, cranes and rigging, excavation, and fire and life safety - governed by OSHA construction (29 CFR 1926) requirements.
Through commissioning you'll manage the safety of energization and testing, and as sites go live you'll transition programs to operational safety under general industry standards (29 CFR 1910), including electrical safety and NFPA 70E, lockout/tagout, and arc flash.
You'll investigate incidents, near misses, and injuries across your sites, drive them to root cause, and follow through on corrective actions - and you'll own EHS record keeping and reporting across the portfolio, including OSHA requirements and any contractor-injury tracking.
You'll be the owner's safety representative in the room with construction and operations partners: reviewing readiness, walking sites, escalating when work isn't safe, and stopping it when it needs to stop.
You'll drive a consistent safety culture across geographically distributed sites and different partner organizations - building emergency preparedness, running or overseeing drills, and making sure lessons from one site reach the others.
You'll select and manage the external support these programs depend on - third-party safety, industrial hygiene, and audit partners - with the EHS Lead's help in setting those relationships up, and you'll contribute to our site design and safety standards so new builds start from a safer baseline.

section_about:
We are hiring an Energy Scheduling & Portfolio Lead to own energy availability across Anthropic's non-cloud data center portfolio: contracted and available energy against planned compute, and the risk to it.
This one central scheduling and portfolio role holds the live view of energy availability risk and energy availability need for workload management.
You will be our counterpart to the LSEs, QSEs, scheduling coordinators, and suppliers in electricity and gas markets across jurisdictions; forecasting is an instrument of that view.
You schedule and manage physical energy delivery - not financial instruments - including how much gas the portfolio needs to schedule, and keep energy supply and the workload plan in step with workload and site planning, energy origination, and data center operations.
ESA counterparties operate the behind-the-meter plants; you manage their performance and our exposure.
This role will also build processes and structures to ultimately support asset management across our energy portfolio.
You are this function's first dedicated owner and will build its models and processes from zero.
section_responsibilities:
Own the live view of energy availability risk and need: contracted, available, and committed energy and capacity at each site against planned load and ramp, by month and by hour where it matters; keep it current as deals sign, sites come online, and plans change, and close gaps and use surpluses with workload and site planning and energy origination.
Be the operational counterpart to our LSEs, QSEs, scheduling coordinators, and retail and wholesale suppliers in domestic ISO/RTOs, including ERCOT, and international power markets, and manage our participation in utility and ISO market programs.
Predict and track curtailment (utility, ISO, fuel, equipment, and contract-driven) for each site, and navigate shortage pricing and reliability events: ISO scarcity pricing, emergency procedures, conservation calls, and the notification and performance obligations under each ESA, PPA, utility agreement, and market program; coordinate the load response with site operations and workload planning, and track performance, compensation, and cost.
Oversee the portfolio's contracted or tariff-based load-flexibility capability and the contribution of this capability to Anthropic's ratepayer-protection commitment: curtailment and demand-response participation, flexible-interconnection and non-firm service commitments to utilities and ISOs, and the site-level playbooks for each; work with workload planning on what the compute can actually flex, and commit only where the workload plan supports it.
For the first operating sites, manage counterparty performance and Anthropic's exposure under the ESAs: outage notices, availability guarantees, liquidated damages, dispatch coordination, and the reporting behind them.
Know the ESAs and utility load agreements we sign well enough to operate their scheduling, curtailment, availability, flexibility, and ratepayer-protection terms, and partner with legal and energy origination so new agreements are operable.
Determine how much gas the portfolio needs to schedule and build the portfolio's gas scheduling strategy for gas-fired behind-the-meter supply, nominations, hub and index pricing, pipeline capacity and constraints, and work through gas-plant outages and their effect on site availability, including by building relationships with external commodity partners.
Build Anthropic's energy forecasting as an instrument of the availability-risk view: consumption per site from the workload plan, site design, and ramp, and cost against ESA and PPA terms, market and natural gas prices, as the monthly and annual outputs the team and Finance need, including exposure to index-priced volume and the inputs energy origination needs to size new supply.
Supply the energy-side inputs and checks that let Finance, Accounting, and Procurement Ops reconcile invoices and settlements against ESA, PPA, and tariff terms and explain the variance; this role will collaborate heavily with energy finance but will not have primary responsibility for financial management of the energy portfolio - the physical position is yours.
Track the market information that moves our position - ISO/RTO prices, scarcity and reliability conditions, gas hub prices, ancillary and capacity costs, and tariff, interconnection, and market rule changes - and reflect it in the view.
Work cross-functionally: with energy finance on the financial management of the portfolio, with data center operations on site load, flexibility, and outages, and with other internal teams - workload and site planning, engineering and design, legal, procurement - so the energy position and the physical reality of each site stay aligned.
Build and own the processes, data, and tooling for all of the above; partner with engineering and site operations on metering, telemetry, and load data so the availability view, forecasts, and settlements rest on measured consumption.
section_requirements:
Have 8+ years in energy markets, power scheduling, energy procurement, or utility / retail energy operations, including hands-on work with scheduling and settlement review in ERCOT, PJM, NYISO, MISO, or another ISO/RTO market.
Have worked at or directly with an LSE, QSE, scheduling coordinator, retail energy provider, or load-management desk, and know day-ahead and real-time scheduling, settlements, and curtailment / demand-response programs from the inside.
Read ESAs, PPAs, and utility large-load interconnection and service agreements fluently enough to operate their scheduling, availability, curtailment, and pricing terms and to model the exposure they create.
Can predict curtailment for a large load and navigate shortage pricing and reliability events - ISO scarcity pricing, emergency procedures, conservation calls - from experience, not from the rulebook.

Experience with data center or other large, fast-ramping load in ERCOT, PJM, NYISO, MISO, or another ISO/RTO market.

Familiarity with hedging and risk management of energy cost - fixed-price, index, shaped, and block products - and with how hedges sit against physical consumption, enough to work fluently with Finance on it.
Familiarity with natural gas markets and hub pricing, with an emphasis on physical scheduling at regional basis hubs, gas-price indices, pipeline nominations and capacity.
Experience with energy data and metering systems, interval data, and building forecasting models from them.
Exposure to the regulatory and public-affairs side of large-load service - large-load tariff proceedings, interconnection rulemakings, or utility rate cases - and to utility and ISO demand-response, curtailment, and flexible-interconnection programs.
Prior experience standing up an operations or analytics function in a growing team.

You will partner closely with energy origination, engineering, demand planning, construction, legal, finance, and third-party development partners to drive equipment availability, establish OEM relationships, and negotiate framework and commercial agreements.
section_responsibilities:
Drive commercial negotiations and framework / Master Purchase Agreements for critical power equipment such as gas turbines (simple and combined cycle), reciprocating engines, fuel cells, large power and generator step-up transformers (HV/EHV), medium- and high-voltage switchgear, substation and protection equipment, solar, and battery energy storage systems.
Secure and manage OEM manufacturing slots and capacity reservations - reservation agreements, deposits, slot allocation, delivery milestones, warranties, liquidated damages, and assignment rights - and run the allocation and reallocation process across sites and regions as deals are signed.
Build and hold relationships with OEM headquarters and regional leadership across North America, Japan and Asia, and Europe, including on capacity-expansion and allocation commitments.
Own the global power equipment strategy: translate the site and energy pipeline into equipment forecasts and procurement pipelines for both off-grid and grid-integrated configurations, and keep the equipment pipeline view (reserved / on order / in fabrication / allocated) current.
Enable innovative power system approaches - off-grid, solar-dominant configurations (solar + BESS with firming) alongside conventional gas + grid - by securing the OEM relationships, reservations, and framework terms that make them buildable at scale and on schedule.
Set the global equipment plan with the regional energy leads in the US, EMEA, and APAC so regional generation strategy, interconnection timelines, and local code and grid requirements are reflected in what is bought, when, and for where.
Decide allocation across sites and partners in constrained markets, hold partners to schedule, and own total cost of supply.
Implement frameworks for ensuring third-party data center partners, EPCs, and general contractors adhere to commercial equipment terms and technical specifications, including owner-furnished equipment (OFE) assignment and reimbursement mechanics.
Work with EPC and power producer / utility counterparties on collaborative sourcing and programmatic equipment approaches - joint or pooled orders, standardized specs, and framework buys that span sites and counterparties - so equipment is bought as a program rather than deal by deal, drawing on utility sourcing practices where they fit.
Own lead-time risk across the portfolio, directing EPCs, development partners, and regional energy leads on lead-time management for long-lead power equipment - tracking OEM lead times and delivery schedules against site and project schedules and deciding order timing and slot allocation and reallocation across sites and counterparties - so equipment lands when each site needs it.

Own the commercial structure (deposits, payment schedules, credit support, capital deployment) with Finance and Legal and carry transactions through executive approval.
Partner with power-system design and engineering early - site power architecture, generation mix, interconnection approach - so equipment sourcing strategy and system design inform each other rather than sourcing arriving after the design is fixed; and on specifications and standardization so equipment purchased on-spec can be redeployed across sites, regions, and development partners.
Negotiate warranty, startup/commissioning support, long-term service, and spare parts terms, and track OEM performance.

Training and serving frontier AI models requires data center capacity at a scale and pace that conventional delivery models were not built for.
Anthropic's Data Center Capacity Delivery team embeds with developers, general contractors, and third-party partners to take leased and partnered sites from deal close through floor access and operational handover as fast as they can safely be built.
As a Regional Manager, you'll own delivery across a regional portfolio of active and upcoming projects.
You'll build and lead the team of Senior Delivery Managers and third-party partners who sit on those sites, set the standards they execute to, and step in yourself where a project needs it.
You are the executive-level interface to our developer partners in the region and the intake point for projects handed over from our transaction team.
This is a highly cross-functional role: you'll work daily with our transaction, design engineering, facility operations and commissioning, deployment, and safety teams, and with developers, GCs, and owner's-representative firms on the ground.
MOC (Mission + Outcomes + Competencies)
Mission
Deliver the region's data center projects to floor access as fast as they can safely be built.
Outcomes
Every active project in the region delivered against early-floor-access and floor-access milestones.
Senior Delivery Manager team hired and led; owner's-rep partners contracted and managed.
Delivery standards (schedule, quality, change control, reporting) enforced across the portfolio.
Executive reporting on progress vs plan and regional capacity projections in place.
Competencies
Senior owner- or GC-side mission-critical delivery leadership.
Builds and leads multi-project teams.
Executive-level developer and GC relationship management.
Leads on site through presence; owns outcomes where no process exists.

You are expected to be on the region's sites enough to shape the culture, approach, and aggressiveness that define the extended teams there - across the portfolio, not one project - and to impact outcomes in a favorable manner.
Be a force multiplier.
Hire, develop, empower, and lead the Senior Delivery Managers on those sites, and raise the skillset developers, contractors, owner's-rep partners, and key trades bring to every project in the region; plan resourcing and headcount as the portfolio grows.
Own portfolio execution for the region - schedule, quality, and safety outcomes on every active project, measured against early-floor-access and floor-access milestones.
You are empowered and have autonomy to own this region's record of performance.
Drive ownership and influence both inside and outside contractual structures: select, scope, contract, and manage owner's-rep and project-management partners; where contracts, incentives, or culture get in the way of speed, change them, and replace partners when performance or culture slips

job_title: Head of Policy Design, Societal Harms
location: United States: San Francisco
section_about:
Anthropic's Safeguards organization builds the policies, evaluations, and detection and enforcement systems that define and hold the limits on how Claude can be used.
In this role, you'll lead our policy design team, managing the teams responsible for radicalization, child safety, user well-being, harmful manipulation, and election integrity, among other harm areas.
The team is responsible for understanding and defining the risks that come with engaging with Claude, how those risks materialize in the real world, and the mitigations needed to prevent them.
As the manager, you'll work with your team to draw the boundaries between what is and is not allowed, then partner with research, product, and engineering to build the right interventions.
Mitigating these harms takes the whole stack: the values and judgment trained into the model itself, the policies and detection systems we enforce on top of it, and the interventions we build into our products.
More capable models, new product surfaces, and new user behaviors will keep testing these boundaries, so the team's policies have to keep pace.
You'll work closely with product to develop and iterate on the strategy and vision for how our safety layers fit together, and with your team and cross-functional partners to decide which mitigations make the most sense and how to implement them.
You'll also coordinate policy decisions across the portfolio: ensuring they're made with the right stakeholders in the room, tracked over time, and applied consistently across harm areas and product surfaces.
This is a leadership role for someone who combines expertise in the harm areas themselves with fluency in how frontier models are actually developed and deployed, and who does their best work across team boundaries.
You'll spend as much time developing the leads who own each harm area as you will on the policy questions themselves.
*Important context for this role: some of the work involves exposure to explicit content, including material of a sexual, violent, or psychologically disturbing nature.
section_responsibilities:
Lead, develop, and grow the managers and teams responsible for the consumer harms portfolio, including child safety, user well-being, harmful manipulation, and election integrity
Coordinate policy decisions across the portfolio, and build the mechanisms that keep them tracked, consistent, and legible - so stakeholders know what was decided, why, and who owns what
Set the strategy for how mitigations built on top of the model - policies, detection and enforcement systems, and product interventions - complement what is trained into the model itself, partnering closely with the alignment training team that owns Claude's character
Prioritize across harm areas competing for the same resources, and make those tradeoffs and their rationale clear to leadership
Serve as the escalation point for high-severity and ambiguous consumer harms decisions, including rapid response to emerging risks
Partner with engineering, data science, product, legal, and research across the model development cycle so consumer harms considerations are represented from training through launch, on every surface where Claude is deployed
Engage external experts, civil society organizations, and regulators, and translate that engagement into stronger policy and enforcement
section_requirements:
Experience leading teams - including managing managers or senior specialists - in AI safety, product policy, or a related field
Deep, applied familiarity with consumer harm areas such as child safety, mental health and well-being, manipulation, or election integrity, and good judgment about how these harms differ in mechanism, severity, and mitigation
A track record of exceptional cross-team collaboration: building durable working relationships with teams you don't control, and getting to shared decisions where ownership is genuinely distributed
Working understanding of how frontier models are developed and deployed - the training and fine-tuning cycle, evaluations, and launch processes - and how different model environments (consumer products, APIs, agentic tools) change both risk and the mitigations available
Experience translating policy positions into mechanisms that can be enforced and measured, and communicating the reasoning to technical and non-technical audiences, including executives
Sound judgment in ambiguous, high-consequence decisions, and comfort making a call and escalating appropriately on incomplete information
section_preferred:
Subject-matter depth in one or more of the portfolio's harm areas, from academia, clinical practice, civil society, government, or trust & safety work
Experience working directly with model training or research teams on model behavior, or shaping the character of a deployed AI system
Experience with generative AI safety systems, including LLM-based classification, evaluation, or enforcement pipelines
Experience engaging external stakeholders in these domains - child safety organizations, election authorities, mental health experts, or regulators
Experience using agentic AI tools to scale a team's analysis and operations

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our Systems team, which builds the real-time infrastructure that classifies the tokens Claude produces and determines whether they are safe to send to users.

location: United States: San Francisco
section_about:
Prompts spec out what Claude does.
Evals measure whether it did.
The Product Prompt and Eval Design team does both for product design: the system prompt that greets a new user, the tool descriptions that decide whether Claude searches, the instructions that keep a slide deck from tipping into slop, and the evals that test all of it.
The point is to keep the model and the product aligned with what users expect, what the product strategy calls for, and what safety requires, on every surface and through every model launch.
This role is a foundational member of that work on the eval side: building the evals that check the prompts, the harness that runs them, and the tools that let designers do this work themselves.
It sits on the Product Prompt and Eval Design team in Product Design, works day to day with the team's surface owners and the engineers in each product team, and pairs per surface with the prompt engineering team at model releases.
section_responsibilities:
Write and revise the prompts behind Claude's tools, features, and behaviors on a product surface; test the surface, turn findings into prompt fixes, ship them, and confirm the prompt users get is the one intended
Build the graders that prove a prompt fix and rerun on the next model; turn designers' hand-run rubrics into automated evals, then read transcripts for what the eval missed
Build visual, low-code eval tools designers can use without an engineer: assemble a comparison set from real transcripts, turn a plain-English rubric into a grader, compare prompt variants across models side by side, and read results in the tool rather than a notebook
Watch designers use those tools and make them simpler
Support model releases: test each surface against the new model, write prompt fixes and migrations, and write prompts for features launching with it, so the surface owner's call has numbers behind it
Stand up and scale the eval harness: build the test environment that exercises our 50 to 100 tools with trustworthy settings, keep evals green across models, and call whether a regression is the harness or the model
Package what prompting can't fix for training, with the eval attached: graders for crisp behaviors, human-feedback questions and good/bad pairs for fuzzy ones like writing quality
section_requirements:
Production-quality Python
Experience building and maintaining evaluation pipelines for LLM products: graders, rubrics, comparison sets, regression suites, and the plumbing that runs them across models
Experience building internal tools with a real interface for people who do not write code
Experience standing up test harnesses, sandboxing tool calls, and pinning the settings that make runs comparable
Experience shipping prompts, or working closely with people who do, and understanding why a prompt that works on one model fails on the next
Reads transcripts, not only scores
section_preferred:
Has worked inside a model-launch cycle
A/B testing experience and the ability to connect offline evals to online outcomes
Front-end or notebook-to-app experience, and opinions about what makes an eval result legible at a glance
Has turned product rubrics into training signal: graders, human-feedback questions, or preference pairs
Cares how Claude behaves for the people using it, not only whether the metric moved

location: United States: San Francisco; United States: New York
section_about:
Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team accelerates the work of organizations doing some of the world's most important under-resourced work: nonprofits, education institutions, scientific researchers, and organizations advancing economic mobility.
Research institutions sit at the center of that mission.
They produce the science the rest of the world builds on, and they are structurally short on time, budget, and technical capacity to figure out new technology on their own.
You will lead our targeted approach to research institutes and research intensive universities globally.
Where our scaled motion reaches thousands of organizations one to many, this role is the opposite end of the same ecosystem: a deliberately short list of institutions where depth matters, where a lab, a department, or a whole campus adopting Claude changes what science gets done, and where the buying process runs through provosts, research offices, procurement, grant budgets, and security review.
Reach comes first, and commercial results follow from it.
That ordering is deliberate and it is shared across every leader on this team: a research institute that adopts Claude to move its science faster is a win on its own terms, and you will be measured on creating that value with the institutions that matter most, not only on pipeline.
You are the single accountable owner for the research Enterprise book globally: its target list, its AEs, its numbers, and its field voice inside Anthropic.
You are half seller, half domain translator.
You will personally run the most complex institutional deals, and you will be credible in a room of scientists and research leaders.
You know how research is funded, how a university decides, and what it takes for a research sales motion to land in a software company.
You will bring that knowledge to the product, applied AI, and marketing teams who build for this audience.
This is a player coach seat.
You will be directly involved in deals and directing the account executives who cover research institutes and universities today, and the role is expected to grow thoughtfully with more AEs in key regions globally.
section_responsibilities:
Co-design our global research strategy: the target list of research institutes and research intensive universities that advance scientific discovery.
Serve as the lead on our most complex institutional deals - setting the pursuit strategy, opening doors with lab and research-office leadership, university provosts, and personally resolving the toughest hurdles: procurement, security review, and grant-funded budgets.
Direct and coach the account executives working research accounts today: joint account plans, deal reviews, and a repeatable motion for landing a university and expanding within it.
Build the institutional playbook: how an institute goes from a pilot to a working deployment across a department, what good adoption looks like, and when to bring in applied AI, customer success, or partners.
Own the book's numbers, institutions reached, activated, and expanded against goals, and use them to decide where the effort goes next.
Work in lockstep with our PLG 1:many motion, so that an institution moves cleanly between scaled programs and direct coverage in both directions.

section_about:
Anthropic's inference engine is the software between the accelerator kernels and the routing layer.
It manages the entire token path in between: batching requests, laying the model out across chips, managing memory for weights and activations, coordinating every forward pass, and managing model state across requests.
Built in-house, it runs on all of our accelerator platforms, serving Claude to millions of users and running our research workloads.
You will work on building and optimizing this system at Anthropic scale: improving throughput, cost, reliability, and latency across all accelerator and cloud platforms.
You are intimately familiar with the hardware and bandwidth numbers (FLOPs, HBM, PCIe, RDMA, network links, etc.) and can model a problem quickly: where the time and bytes go, and what sets the bound.
The role is deeply technical and high-impact, and suits engineers who enjoy working across accelerator programming, high-performance systems that seamlessly coordinate between host and device, and large-scale distributed systems.
Familiarity with the transformer architecture is a plus.
Some example recurring themes:
Keep device utilization high.
Accelerators should never be waiting due to other overheads.
Reuse instead of recompute.
Keep model state cached and reuse it whenever that is cheaper than computing it again.
Measure, model, then change.
We build the observability to see where the gaps are, model the impact of potential improvements, deploy them, and go around again, with Claude speeding up every turn of that loop.
Tokens you can trust.
Ensuring model quality matters more than efficiency.
We build the infrastructure to ensure Claude maintains its intelligence across platforms and over time.
Safety on every token.
We work closely with our safeguards and safety teams.
The inference engine is the backbone behind our production safety systems, ensuring efficiency without compromising robustness.

section_about:
As an Accommodations Partner at Anthropic, you will own the end-to-end reasonable accommodation process, ensuring employees and candidates receive fair, compliant, and thoughtful support.
You will serve as the subject matter expert on complex, high-stakes accommodation requests and applicable disability law across the jurisdictions where Anthropic operates, leading the interactive process with employees, managers, and HR, and partnering closely with Recruiting (for candidates), Benefits, Employment Legal, and external partners to identify effective solutions.
This role requires balancing hands-on casework with process-building, as you will manage individual accommodation requests directly while also helping shape the frameworks, documentation, and cross-functional coordination needed to scale this function globally.
You'll partner closely with People Partners, Benefits, Recruiting, Employment Legal, and Occupational Health resources across regions to navigate sensitive medical and disability-related matters with care, discretion, and sound judgment.
As we continue to scale rapidly, you'll help build the foundations of an accommodations function that can grow with the organization.
section_responsibilities:
Interactive Process Management - U.S.:
Serve as the primary point of contact for reasonable accommodation requests from U.S.-based employees and candidates, leading the interactive process from initial request through resolution.
Partner directly with employees, managers, People Partners, and recruiters to understand functional limitations, evaluate potential accommodations, and reach determinations that are both legally sound and operationally workable.
Global Accommodation Request Management:
Own accommodation requests from employees and candidates outside of the United States, serving as the initial point of contact and primary owner, in partnership with regional People Partners and Employment Legal.
Complex Case Management:
Own complex, high-stakes, or legally ambiguous accommodation requests personally, including those involving conflicting medical documentation, competing business needs, or heightened legal risk, while providing guidance to People Partners and managers on more straightforward cases.
Cross-Functional Partnership:
Partner closely with the internal Benefits team on accommodation requests intersecting with leave, disability, or benefits eligibility.
Interface with external partners, including accommodation platform vendors, to support timely and accurate case review.
Policy & Program Development:
Along with the broader ER/People team, build scalable, repeatable processes and documentation for accommodation requests across regions.
Develop frameworks that support consistent, defensible decision-making while remaining responsive to the nuance of individual cases.
Education & Enablement:
Own education strategy for accommodations best practices, delivering training and guidance to People Partners, managers, and interviewers, and on how to support the process appropriately while maintaining confidentiality.
Documentation & Recordkeeping:
Ensure accommodation requests, supporting materials, and determinations are documented and handled appropriately, maintaining accurate records, files, and confidentiality throughout the process.
Data & Insights:
Track accommodation metrics and trends to identify patterns, inform policy decisions, and proactively flag systemic issues or risk areas.

location: United Kingdom: London
section_about:
Anthropic's consulting and systems integration partners now sell and deliver Claude work at growing volume, and selling alongside partners is working.
What matters next is delivery: whether the partner completes the work, whether the customer's Claude usage grows and holds, and whether the outcome is good enough that the customer asks for that partner again.
The Partner Success Lead owns that outcome.
You will hold a book of in-flight customer engagements across a set of managed partners in EMEA.
From the day our Partner Delivery program matches a customer engagement to a partner in your book, you own it to a completed outcome: the work finishes on scope, the customer's Claude usage grows, and a stalled engagement gets diagnosed and unblocked before the customer disengages.
You wake up every day on one question: what is each partner in my book doing, and is the work getting done.
section_responsibilities:
Own every customer engagement in your book from partner match to completed outcome.
Know the state of each one every week: scope, timeline, blockers, and the customer's Claude usage trend.
Run the weekly delivery review across your book, and bring stalled or at-risk engagements to the weekly at-risk account review with a diagnosis, an owner, and a specific ask rather than a status list.
Unblocking.
Partner capacity, scope creep, customer readiness, product questions, deal-registration conflicts, and customer dissatisfaction with partner work: get each issue to the right internal team and stay on it through resolution.
Own delivery quality and consumption across your book.
Track engagements completed on time, time from match to completion, delivered consumption and weekly active use on the customer accounts your partners serve, and the accounts trending toward at-risk.
Build senior relationships with each managed partner's practice and delivery leadership.
Together with the Partner Account Manager and other Anthropic counterparts, establish the executive-level trust that lets you ask a partner to restaff, escalate, or invest - and be taken seriously - when an engagement needs it.
Build each partner's Claude practice as the compounding work: certified bench depth, one repeatable offering in a chosen industry lane, and a published customer story from each completed engagement, so the next engagement needs less from you.
Turn what works into methodology.
Convert the moves you prove in your book into named, reusable best practices - engagement review packs, unblocking plays, practice-building guides - written clearly enough to be shared at scale across partners, the Partner Success team, and the contract delivery team running the same loop.
Run the quarterly practice review with each managed partner's alliance and delivery leads: joint goals on completed customer engagements, customer adoption, certified practitioners, references, and industry positioning.
Present and persuade across audiences.
Deliver partner executive briefings, practitioner enablement sessions, and internal reviews with equal command - this role is regularly the voice of Partner Success in front of a partner's leadership, a delivery team, a customer, or Anthropic's own leadership.
Steward funding requests from partners in your book.
Recommend for or against co-investment and program funding requests against a stated outcome, and reconcile against milestones.
The bar is outcomes, not consultant hours.
Work the handoffs cleanly: from Partner Sales when a partner deal closes, and from the Partner Delivery program when an engagement is matched to a partner in your book.
Coordinate with the Partner Account Manager on any strategic partner that has one, with Customer Success Managers on customer-side account health, and with Anthropic's direct sales field on joint accounts.
Instrument your book and know its numbers: engagements in flight and completed, stall rate and days to unblock, delivered consumption per partner, certified practitioner counts, and partner health trajectory.
Run your book Claude-first.
Telemetry drafts the diagnosis; you validate it and act.
Claude drafts your review packs, status notes, and escalation briefs; you own the judgment, the exceptions, and the unblocking.
Feed what you see in the field back into the packages, playbooks, tier rules, and health rubric the team runs on.
section_requirements:
Experience owning a high-volume book of concurrent customer engagements, projects, or accounts (roughly 10 to 30 at a time) to completed outcomes, in a partner success, customer success, delivery management, or technical account management role.
Ability and appetite to build structure, clarity, and programmatic motions out of in-flight work, while delivering engagement by engagement.
You have written something down - a review format, a checklist, a play - that others ran without you, and you want to do more of that; growing that into the operating playbook a wider team runs is the senior end of this role, not the entry bar.
This role scales by what you write down, not by added hours.
Track record of a number tied to completed work and customer behavior (on-time delivery, adoption, retention, consumption, expansion) rather than contract signature, and an operating rhythm you built to hit it.
Judgment on delivery quality: you can review a partner's engagement plan or scope and tell whether it will finish on time and produce usage, and you ask the follow-up question that surfaces the real risk.
Escalation and unblocking judgment across a matrix (partner, customer, direct sales, customer success, product): you know which stall belongs to whom, you get help fast, and you stay engaged to resolution.
A convincing speaker and presenter to all kinds of audiences: partner executives, delivery practitioners, customers, and internal leadership.
You can carry a quarterly practice review, an enablement session, and an executive escalation in the same week and land each one.
Deep understanding of how customer success works in a usage-based business; you have held a number tied to customer behavior and can read a consumption trend and act on it.
Enough technical fluency to be credible in a delivery review.

Active daily use of Claude or another large language model as part of how you work: preparing reviews, drafting account plans, and analyzing your book.

Depth in a specific industry vertical (financial services, healthcare, public sector, retail, or manufacturing) where you have carried a book of partners or customers.

location: United States: Washington
section_about:
We are hiring a National Security Partnerships Lead to grow and manage our relationships with the U.S.
Intelligence Community and with allied intelligence and security services.
You will report to the Head of National Security Policy and advise company leadership on intelligence and allied-partner matters.
You will help partner security organizations build policies that let them adopt frontier AI quickly and for high-impact missions, while deploying it safely and avoiding incidents.
You will also engage U.S. and foreign government officials on the policy frameworks that guide the international distribution and deployment of Anthropic's models.
You will own a portfolio of government partnerships end to end: setting the agenda with senior counterparts, structuring the agreements and channels that govern each relationship, and bringing partner requirements and concerns back into Anthropic's policy, product, research, and safeguards decisions.
You will work closely with our public sector sales, legal, security, and threat intelligence teams.
section_responsibilities:
Lead Anthropic's strategic engagement with U.S.
Intelligence Community elements and allied intelligence and security services.
Help partner security organizations develop the policies and governance that enable rapid, high-impact adoption of frontier AI and safe deployments that avoid incidents.
Identify high-leverage national security deployments with partners, and support our public sector sales team in delivering them.
Brief senior government security officials in the U.S. and allied capitals on frontier AI capabilities, risks, and Anthropic's approach to safety.
Engage U.S. and foreign government officials on the national security implications of the international distribution and deployment of Anthropic's models, and advise company leadership on partner equities in those decisions.
Partner with federal affairs, international policy, communications, and marketing on national security matters, including engagement with the Executive Branch and Congress.
Travel regularly within the U.S. and to allied countries.

Direct experience managing relationships with foreign partner governments or services.

Experience negotiating formal agreements or partnerships between governments, or between government and industry.

10+ years of experience in national security, including substantial work in or with the Intelligence Community.
Experience in a liaison, foreign partnership, or foreign disclosure role.
Experience in related private-sector roles, such as at technology, cybersecurity, or defense companies.
Regional expertise or language skills relevant to allied partners.
Hands-on familiarity with large language models and how they can be misused.

section_about:
At Anthropic, we're building AI systems that are safe, beneficial, and transformative.
Our mission is to develop AI that benefits humanity, and we believe the most powerful capabilities emerge when we thoughtfully bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and real-world applications.
Frontier AI runs on datacenters, and the world is in the middle of the largest infrastructure buildout in a generation.
The binding constraint on progress is increasingly everything around the chips: land, power, permits, equipment, and the design and construction of the buildings themselves.
Bringing a single site online involves hundreds of people, thousands of components, and decisions that move enormous amounts of capital.
Much of that work still runs on spreadsheets and handoffs.
At Anthropic, we're building software and Claude-powered tools to help Anthropic scale out its compute, and we think there's an enormous opportunity to rethink how that work gets done.
It's early, it's already having a real impact, and the engineers who join now will shape how one of the most consequential buildouts in the world gets done.
We're looking for strong, versatile software engineers who love building for people doing real work in the physical world.
You'll embed with the teams that source sites, design buildings, procure equipment, and manage construction, learn their work deeply, and build the tools and systems they rely on every day.
Datacenter experience is a big plus, but what matters most is that you can earn the trust of expert operators, model a messy domain cleanly, and move fast.
section_responsibilities:
Build the core systems that track a datacenter's lifecycle (sites, designs, bills of materials, equipment, and construction progress) in one trusted, permissioned source of truth
Embed with datacenter, energy, and supply chain teams to understand how the work actually gets done, find the critical path, and build the tools they reach for first
Bring order to messy data by migrating and reconciling spreadsheets and legacy trackers, and integrate with the industry's tools, like construction management, scheduling, and engineering systems
Design for trust: fine-grained permissions, auditability, and data quality for information that steers major investment decisions
Ship early, iterate with users, and cut anything that doesn't help bring compute online sooner
Partner with research to understand new model capabilities and share where they fall short in engineering-heavy, physical-world domains

Have built software that teams in a physical-world industry depend on, such as datacenters, construction, energy, manufacturing, supply chain, or logistics
Have a track record of zero-to-one work in startup or startup-like environments
Are deeply user-centric: you learn the domain from the people doing the work and validate with them before over-investing
Bring high agency and good judgment about what matters, and hold strong opinions loosely

section_about:
Anthropic's Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team is the connective tissue that holds the company accountable to its security commitments.
We translate regulatory, customer, and voluntary obligations into controls that teams act on, and give leadership a bird's-eye view of how well we're meeting them.
We're building toward a fundamentally different kind of GRC: one that directs Claude, with the right humans in the loop, to challenge and evidence the performance of controls continuously rather than through periodic audits.
Within Security GRC, Compliance & Audit Programs run the integrated audit across our frameworks and maintains the Common Control Framework, the single set of controls that the whole program is built on.
This role sits in Audit & Assurance and owns the framework and the assurance view across every control domain.
As part of the Security Audit & Controls team, you will own the CCF across every control domain, from access and change management to logging, encryption, and people controls: which controls we have, what each one says, how each maps to the frameworks and commitments we hold, and whether each one is actually working.
You'll work with control owners and GRC Partners to draft and validate control descriptions and activities that describe reality rather than policy intent, build the monitoring that shows operating effectiveness continuously instead of once a year, and drive what monitoring finds to closure with control owners.
Building with Claude is a normal part of the job: drafting and mapping controls, testing evidence, and monitoring control health, with you deciding where human judgment stays in the loop.
This is an individual contributor role for someone who works well independently, writes clearly, and gets satisfaction from a control set that is accurate, tested, and trusted by auditors and engineers alike.
section_responsibilities:
Own the Common Control Framework: the canonical control set, its mappings to SOC 2, ISO 27001/42001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and customer commitments, and the change process for adding, retiring, or rewording controls
Draft and validate control descriptions and control activities with control owners, so each control states who does what, how often, in which system, and what evidence proves it
Design and run continuous monitoring of control efficacy: define the metrics and automated tests that show operating effectiveness, tune out false positives, surface failures to owners before an auditor does, and build the controls maturity model that shows where each control domain stands and what it takes to move up a level
Verify remediation and carry it into steady state:
GRC Partners lead remediation in their domains and control owners implement the fixes.
This role advises on control design and implementation, confirms fixes against what the auditor actually asked for, and keeps one source of truth for control and finding status.
Once a fix holds, it works with the partner to standardize the evidence pull and, where appropriate, automate it or build continuous monitoring, so the control rolls into the unified audit management program.
Map new frameworks and commitments onto the CCF as we commit to them, and support gap assessments when a new framework, certification, product, or entity comes into scope, using the CCF as the baseline and writing the requirements for each delta
Support the integrated audit and customer audits: readiness checks, walkthrough preparation, evidence request lists, and the readout of external findings back to GRC
Evaluate evidence reliability, including the completeness and accuracy of system-generated reports and AI-generated evidence, and set the standard for what audit-ready evidence looks like here
Build with Claude: automate control mapping, evidence testing, and monitoring, and verify machine-drafted control language before it becomes the record

section_about:
At Anthropic, we're building AI systems that are safe, beneficial, and transformative.
Our mission is to develop AI that benefits humanity, and we believe the most powerful capabilities emerge when we thoughtfully bridge the gap between research breakthroughs and real-world applications.
Claude is getting good at research.
Given a well-posed problem, it can read the literature, write and run simulations, analyze results, and iterate on a design across physics, materials, chemistry, and engineering.
But most of the hardest problems in science and engineering aren't well-posed.
They live inside companies and labs with their own data, tools, constraints, and experts, and progress depends on turning all of that into work a model can actually do and check.
Our Applied AI, Science & Engineering team takes Claude to the scientists and engineers working on hard problems in energy, materials, hardware design, and other physical-world fields.
We build the tools Claude needs to do real research and engineering work.
Mostly that means software: the agent harnesses, integrations, evaluations, and working processes that turn a partner's problem into something Claude can make progress on and validate.
We find real-world problems and test what we build through partner engagements, then feed our learnings back to our research and product teams.
It's early, and the engineers who join now will shape how Claude gets applied to science and engineering.
This is an engineering role first.
You'll spend real time with domain experts, become the person who knows how to get Claude working in their field, and prototype quickly alongside them.
Most of your time, though, goes into building and hardening the systems that make that work repeatable, not into writing recommendations or configuring someone else's product.
A science or engineering background is a big plus, but what matters most is that you can earn the trust of expert researchers, turn a fuzzy problem into something concrete and checkable, and ship.

Build the agent harnesses and research loops that let Claude carry a problem from literature review through hypothesis generation, simulation, analysis, and design iteration
Connect scientific computing and simulation tools (finite element, CFD, electromagnetic, or molecular modeling codes, for example) so Claude can drive them reliably and at scale
Design and build evaluations that tell us whether Claude's work is actually right, and be honest about where it isn't
Sit with scientists and engineers at partner organizations to learn their problem, data, tools, and constraints, and turn open-ended questions into well-specified, verifiable tasks with clear success criteria
Prototype with partners, ship pilots into their workflows, and cut anything that doesn't move the problem forward
Turn what works in one engagement into shared tools, reusable components, and documented processes the next one can start from
Be the technical voice on how Claude performs on science and engineering work, explaining results, limits, and tradeoffs clearly to researchers, engineering leads, and non-technical stakeholders alike
Partner with our research and product teams to share where models fall short on science and engineering work, and help shape what comes next

En tant qu'Enterprise Account Executive chez Anthropic, vous rejoindrez l'équipe fondatrice chargée de faire découvrir notre API de productivité IA de pointe et nos solutions SaaS aux entreprises du secteur de la distribution et du commerce en France.
Vous favoriserez l'adoption d'une IA de pointe et sûre en concluant des contrats stratégiques avec des entreprises de la distribution, de la grande distribution alimentaire, de la mode et de l'e-commerce.
Vous mettrez à profit votre expertise de la vente consultative dans le secteur du retail pour accélérer la croissance du chiffre d'affaires.
Vous nouerez aussi des relations de confiance avec les parties prenantes du secteur et les aiderez à intégrer et à déployer l'IA, tout en leur faisant découvrir l'étendue de ses capacités dans le merchandising et la supply chain, l'exploitation des magasins, l'e-commerce et le marketing, et le service client.
En collaboration avec les équipes GTM, Produit et Marketing, vous affinerez en continu notre proposition de valeur, notre méthodologie de vente et notre positionnement, afin qu'ils trouvent un écho auprès des instances décisionnelles du secteur du retail.
Le profil idéal a à cœur de développer de nouveaux segments de marché, de repérer les opportunités à fort potentiel et de mettre en œuvre les stratégies qui permettent de les saisir.
En favorisant le déploiement des produits émergents d'Anthropic, vous aiderez les entreprises à acquérir de nouvelles capacités tout en contribuant au développement éthique de l'IA.

Remporter de nouveaux contrats et générer du chiffre d'affaires pour Anthropic dans le secteur du retail.
Vous orienter au sein d'organisations complexes pour atteindre les personnes décisionnaires clés, leur présenter nos services et les aider à réussir avec Anthropic.
Vous piloterez l'intégralité du cycle de vente, de la première prise de contact à la signature.
Concevoir et mettre en œuvre des stratégies commerciales innovantes, adaptées aux cycles d'achat, aux calendriers commerciaux et aux processus budgétaires du retail, afin d'atteindre et de dépasser les objectifs de chiffre d'affaires.
Analyser le paysage, les tendances et les dynamiques du marché du retail pour traduire les plans stratégiques en actions et campagnes commerciales ciblées.
Piloter l'expansion sur le marché en identifiant de nouveaux cas d'usage au sein des équipes merchandising et supply chain, de l'exploitation des magasins, des fonctions e-commerce et marketing, et du service client.
Collaborer de manière transverse pour différencier nos offres destinées aux applications du retail.
Naviguer dans des écosystèmes complexes de parties prenantes (direction générale, directions métiers et opérations, DSI et services achats) afin de construire un consensus.
Contribuer à la feuille de route et aux fonctionnalités produit en recueillant les retours des équipes utilisatrices du secteur et en relayant les besoins du marché.
Apporter des éclairages qui renforcent notre proposition de valeur pour le retail.
Affiner en continu la méthodologie de vente dédiée au retail en intégrant les enseignements dans des playbooks, des modèles et des bonnes pratiques.
Identifier des améliorations de processus qui optimisent la productivité et la cohérence commerciales.

Une expérience confirmée du dépassement des objectifs de chiffre d'affaires, grâce à une gestion efficace d'un pipeline et d'un processus de vente en constante évolution
D'excellentes compétences en communication et l'aisance nécessaire pour présenter devant des publics variés du retail, des équipes opérationnelles et digitales jusqu'aux membres de la direction
Une connaissance approfondie des cycles d'achat, des processus de décision et des principales problématiques du secteur du retail
Une approche stratégique et analytique du marché du retail, alliée à une exécution tactique et créative pour saisir les opportunités
